articles.title: Grand Slam of Darts tables and permutations: What Luke Littler, Luke Humphries and more need to progress to last 16
articles.summary: Luke Littler, Luke Humphries, Nathan Aspinall and Rusty-Jake Rodriguez can all qualify for the last 16 with high-scoring defeats in the final group games; watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports with the final on Sunday November 22
articles.body:
The 48-player field is split into 16 groups of three with only one going through, meaning each player has only two pool matches to try and earn a place in the second round.

Monday sees the conclusion of Groups A-H with Groups I-P to be concluded on Tuesday.

Read on to see how Luke Littler, Luke Humphries and Nathan Aspinall can all lose their final matches and still qualify for the last 16...

Sat Nov 14: Luke Littler 5-2 Beau Greaves

Sun Nov 15: Niels Zonneveld 3-5 Beau Greaves

Mon Nov 16: Luke Littler v Niels Zonneveld

Luke Littler can afford to lose to Niels Zonneveld on Monday night and still have a chance of progressing.

The Nuke simply needs to win three legs to reach the last 16 with Zonneveld needing to win 5-2 or better to reach the knockout stages.

Beau Greaves is one of the few players to be eliminated despite winning one of her matches.

Sat Nov 14: Jermaine Wattimena 5-2 Lisa Ashton

Mon Nov 16: Jermaine Wattimena v Alan Soutar

Lisa Ashton has been eliminated after losing both of her first two matches, which means whoever wins Monday's match between Jermaine Wattimena and Alan Soutar will reach the last 16.

Eighth seed Josh Rock has been eliminated after two defeats, which means whoever wins the Kevin Doets v Tommy Morris clash on Monday will qualify for the knockout round.

Sat Nov 14: Stephen Bunting 5-4 Raymond Smith

Sun Nov 15: Cameron Menzies 5-4 Raymond Smith

Mon Nov 16: Stephen Bunting v Cameron Menzies

Two last-leg defeats mean that Raymond Smith has been eliminated from the competition. Cameron Menzies will face Stephen Bunting in a winner-goes-through decider on Monday.

Sun Nov 15: Sebastian Bialecki 5-4 Joe Hunt

Mon Nov 16: Gerwyn Price v Sebastian Bialecki

Joe Hunt crashed out after losing both of his match, so Gerwyn Price and Sebastian Bialecki will clash on Monday night with the winner reaching the knockout rounds.

Sat Nov 14: Ryan Searle 5-4 Charlie Manby

Sun Nov 15: Andrew Gilding 5-4 Charlie Manby

Mon Nov 16: Ryan Searle v Andrew Gilding

Charlie Manby has been eliminated from the competition after suffering two last-leg defeats, meaning the victor in Monday's clash between Ryan Searle and Andrew Gilding will secure a spot in the last 16.

Sat Nov 14: Jonny Clayton 4-5 Anton Ostlund

Jonny Clayton was the highest-ranked player to be knocked out of the tournament on Sunday, meaning Rob Cross and Anton Ostlund will face off on Tuesday with the winner qualifying.

Sat Nov 14: Wessel Nijman 5-1 Adam Sevada

Sun Nov 15: Niko Springer 5-1 Adam Sevada

Mon Nov 16: Wessel Nijman v Niko Springer

Adam Sevada has been eliminated after two 5-1 losses, meaning the winner of Wessel Nijman vs Niko Springer on Monday night will reach the last 16.

Sat Nov 14: Luke Humphries 5-3 Paolo Nebrida

Sun Nov 15: Joe Cullen 2-5 Paolo Nebrida

In Group I, all three players are still in the tournament.

Luke Humphries needs to win four or five legs against Joe Cullen on Monday night to reach the last 16. A 5-4 defeat would still be enough for him to qualify.

Cullen must win that match 5-0 to get through - while Paolo Nebrida will reach the last 16 if Cullen wins by a scoreline of 5-1, 5-2 or 5-3.

Sat Nov 14: Luke Woodhouse 3-5 Tom Sykes

Sun Nov 15: Luke Woodhouse 1-5 Krzysztof Ratajski

Tue Nov 17: Krzysztof Ratajski v Tom Sykes

Luke Woodhouse became the first seed to be eliminated from the competition as he lost both of his group matches. Whoever wins Tuesday night's match between Krzysztof Ratajski and Tom Sykes will therefore qualify for the knockout rounds.

Sat Nov 14: James Wade 5-1 Cameron Crabtree

Sun Nov 15: Ricky Evans 5-4 Cameron Crabtree

Cam Crabtree was beaten in both of his Group K matches, which means this is another pool where the final match will decide the winner. James Wade will take on Ricky Evans on Tuesday with the winner going through.

Sat Nov 14: Michael van Gerwen 5-4 Henry Coates

Sun Nov 15: Jeffrey de Graaf 4-5 Henry Coates

Tue Nov 17: Michael van Gerwen v Jeffrey de Graaf

This is the group where things could get very interesting with all three players still in contention to top the group.

Any sort of win for Michael van Gerwen on Tuesday will see him qualify for the last 16. However, a victory of 5-3 or better would see Jeffrey de Graaf take top spot.

If De Graaf was to beat Van Gerwen 5-4 then Henry Coates would still be in the mix as all three players would be tied.

The group would then be decided on legs won against throw and then the highest total tournament average (to two decimal places).

Sat Nov 14: Gian van Veen 5-2 Carl Sneyd

Sun Nov 15: Bradley Brooks 5-3 Carl Sneyd

Tue Nov 17: Gian van Veen v Bradley Brooks

Group M is another group where the final match is a straight shoot-out for a place in the last 16. That match will take place between Gian van Veen and Bradley Brooks after Carl Sneyd was eliminated following two defeats in his first two matches.

Sun Nov 15: Martin Schindler 5-0 Jan Schmidt

Tue Nov 17: Chris Dobey v Martin Schindler

Jan Schmidt lost both of his matches to drop out of the tournament, which means it's a straight shootout between Chris Dobey and Martin Schindler on Tuesday night to see who tops the group.

Sat Nov 14: Ross Smith 3-5 Rusty-Jake Rodriguez

Sun Nov 15: Ross Smith 5-4 Gabriel Clemens

Tue Nov 17: Gabriel Clemens v Rusty-Jake Rodriguez

Gabriel Clemens is one of the few players to have lost a match but can still qualify for the last 16. He must beat Rusty-Jake Rodriguez 5-3 or better to top Group O.

Rusty-Jake Rodriguez simply needs to win four legs to qualify. A victory of a 5-4 defeat would be enough for him.

Group O favourite Ross Smith has already been eliminated, but can still finish second in the group if Rodriguez wins Tuesday's final match.

Sat Nov 14: Nathan Aspinall 5-1 Maik Kuivenhoven

Sun Nov 15: Karel Sedlacek 4-5 Maik Kuivenhoven

Tue Nov 17: Nathan Aspinall v Karel Sedlacek

Nathan Aspinall doesn't even need to win on Tuesday night. He will qualify if he wins just three legs against Karel Sedlacek.

After throwing away a 4-1 advantage against Maik Kuivenhoven, Karel Sedlacek knows he must beat Aspinall 5-2 or better if he wants to reach the next round.

Kuivenhoven has been eliminated from the tournament but will finish second in the group if Aspinall wins.

Instead of eight groups of four, the expanded 48-player field is now split into 16 groups of three.

Rather than the top two in each group progressing like in previous editions, only the top player from each group will progress.

In the group stage, two points will be awarded for a win, and no points are awarded for a defeat.

Should there be a three-way points tie in any group after the round-robin games have been played, these would be split as follows:

Highest total tournament average (to two decimal places)

Highest winning match average (to two decimal places)

If players cannot be split after the above criteria, a play-off will be organised between the players at the end of the session in which the final group game is played and will be a two or three-way nine-dart shootout in which the player scoring the most points is deemed the winner.

The order of throw would be determined by PDC ranking, with the highest ranked player having the option to throw first, second, or third.

articles.title: Claudia Fernández sacó tres veces seguidas… ¡y nadie se dio cuenta!
articles.standfirst: La madrileña sirvió en el turno de su compañera durante el arranque de la final del P1 de Dubái sin que el juez de silla o sus rivales advirtieran el error
articles.summary: La madrileña sirvió en el turno de su compañera durante el arranque de la final del P1 de Dubái sin que el juez de silla o sus rivales advirtieran el error
articles.body: Una situación nada habitual se produjo en la final del P1 de Dubái de Premier Padel. Claudia Fernández y Martina Calvo conquistaron el título ante Paula Josemaría y Bea González por 7-5 y 6-1, pero más allá de la contundente victoria de la joven dupla española, el encuentro dejó una anécdota reglamentaria insólita al comienzo del choque de la que nadie en la pista se percató. La ‘Niña Maravilla’ sirvió en los tres primeros turnos de su pareja y el partido siguió su curso con total normalidad. Al igual que ocurre en el tenis y en los partidos de dobles, el servicio va alternándose entre ambas duplas en cada juego. Esa regla básica sí se respetó sin fallos. El problema llegó en la rotación interna de Claudia y Martina: tras el primer saque de una jugadora y el posterior turno de las rivales, le correspondía servir a su compañera. Sin embargo, debido a un despiste generalizado tanto de las cuatro protagonistas como del juez de silla, Fernández puso la pelota en juego en las tres primeras ocasiones que le tocó sacar a su equipo, provocando que Calvo no estrenara su servicio hasta el séptimo juego del primer set. Arrancó Claudia el partido al saque, colocando el 1-0 inicial. Hasta ahí, todo dentro de lo previsto. Acto seguido fue el turno de Paula y Bea, que cumplieron con el guion habitual para igualar la contienda. Una vez concluido ese segundo juego, el reglamento dictaba que debía sacar Martina Calvo con 1-1 en el luminoso. No obstante, volvió a ser la madrileña quien se colocó tras la línea de fondo sin que ninguna de las presentes ni el árbitro detuvieran el juego. Fernández sacó adelante su servicio para el 2-1 y, tras el turno de Josemaría y González para el 2-2, llegó el quinto juego del set. En ese momento sí correspondía por rotación natural el turno de Claudia Fernández, quien volvió a ponerse al servicio por tercera vez consecutiva para su pareja tras haberse saltado el turno de su compañera. Tres servicios seguidos de la jugadora de drive sin que saltara ninguna alarma en la pista central de Dubái. Hubo que esperar hasta el séptimo juego para que la navarra tomara por fin las riendas del saque, poniendo fin a una de las curiosidades más llamativas de la temporada. En el pádel profesional, donde cada detalle suele estar milimetrado por los jueces de silla y los propios equipos, resulta muy poco habitual que un fallo en la rotación del servicio pase inadvertido durante tantos juegos. Sin embargo, al no producirse ninguna reclamación ni advertencia arbitral durante el desarrollo de la manga, el orden quedó validado sobre la marcha y Claudia y Martina terminaron levantando su tercer trofeo juntas en dos sets sin que este curioso despiste empañara su triunfo.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy fights back tears after revealing family health issue
articles.summary: After wrapping up his record-tying eighth championship, Rory McIlroy revealed his father has been hospitalized while recovering from surgery.
articles.body:
Rory McIlroy earns a second green jacket at the 2026 Masters

Rory McIlroy got emotional after wrapping up a record-tying eighth career Race to Dubai championship .

After equaling Colin Montgomerie's eight European Tour Order of Merit titles by virtue of his second-place finish in the season-ending DP World Championship, McIlroy revealed that his father is in the process of recovering from major surgery.

"He's been in the hospital for the last two months. He underwent a huge operation at the end of September, and he's recovering well, thankfully," McIlroy said.

At that point, he paused and covered his eyes with his hands, while taking a moment to compose himself.

McIlroy said he went to see his father in Cleveland before leaving for Dubai to play in the DP World Championship and his dad told him, "Go win the Race to Dubai."

McIlroy, 37, shot a bogey-free 67 in the final round to finish five strokes behind winner Tyrell Hatton. His second-place finish secured his fifth consecutive season-long title on the DP World Tour, formerly known as the European Tour.

articles.title: Los escalofriantes audios de la esposa de Juan De Bedout sobre el talio antes de morir
articles.standfirst: Caso talio en Bogotá: revelan audios de Alicia Graham, esposa de Juan de Bedout, sobre su intoxicación
articles.summary: Caso talio en Bogotá: revelan audios de Alicia Graham, esposa de Juan de Bedout, sobre su intoxicación
articles.body: El caso que conmocionó a Colombia por el envenenamiento masivo con talio —un metal altamente tóxico, imperceptible y letal— ha dado un giro tan inesperado como escalofriante. La Unidad Investigativa de El Tiempo sacó a la luz pública los registros y audios inéditos que dejó Alicia Graham Sardi, esposa del economista y empresario Juan de Bedout Vargas, antes de fallecer el 17 de agosto de 2021. Las grabaciones revelan una angustiosa verdad silenciada durante años: semanas antes de su muerte, oficializada en su momento como producto de un cáncer terminal, la mujer estaba convencida de que alguien la estaba envenenando sistemáticamente con el mismo metal pesado que, trágicamente, años después cobraría la vida de su propia hija. Los audios a los que tuvo acceso el medio periodístico —y que hoy reposan en la denuncia formal presentada ante la Fiscalía General de la Nación por los hermanos de la víctima, Carlos y Cristina Graham Sardi, bajo la representación del penalista David Espinosa Acuña— muestran el progresivo deterioro físico y psicológico de Alicia Graham. En una de las grabaciones clave, fechada el 29 de julio de 2021, la mujer pronunció una frase lapidaria: “Otra vez me están envenenando”. A medida que su salud empeoraba dentro de su residencia y centros médicos en Bogotá, Graham advirtió con firmeza que la sustancia le era suministrada de manera deliberada en la capital colombiana. Lo que hacía más desconcertante el cuadro clínico en aquel entonces era el contraste geográfico de sus síntomas: sus registros personales y médicos evidenciaban que su condición mejoraba ostensiblemente cada vez que salía de Bogotá, ya fuera disfrutando de unas vacaciones de Semana Santa en Cartagena o viajando al exterior para aplicarse la vacuna contra el covid-19. Ante la sospecha de que alguien de su círculo íntimo atentaba contra su vida, Alicia intentó desesperadamente contratar los servicios de un investigador privado para someter a su entorno a pruebas de polígrafo y revisar antecedentes. Sin embargo, el rápido avance de su enfermedad y su fallecimiento, ocurrido en la Fundación Santa Fe de Bogotá, truncaron la gestión antes de que pudiera esclarecer la verdad. El núcleo de la denuncia penal radica en un elemento crucial que, según los denunciantes, no fue debidamente visibilizado en el expediente clínico original: un examen de orina de 24 horas practicado a Alicia Graham el 3 de agosto de 2021 —dos semanas antes de su deceso—, el cual arrojó 672,9 microgramos de talio por litro, un nivel crítico de intoxicación por este elemento químico inodoro, incoloro e insípido. A pesar de que el resultado fue remitido desde el laboratorio al centro médico, la familia denuncia que no figuraba de manera transparente en la historia clínica oficial y que, tras su muerte, el cuerpo de Alicia fue rápidamente cremado, impidiendo una necropsia forense rigurosa que determinara el papel real del metal pesado en su fallecimiento, catalogado oficialmente como un cáncer terminal. Este expediente se cruza de manera tétrica con el magnicidio y envenenamiento de tres adolescentes en abril de 2025, entre quienes se encontraba Inés de Bedout, hija de Juan de Bedout y de la fallecida Alicia Graham, quienes consumieron frambuesas contaminadas con talio dentro de la misma dinámica familiar. Por ese caso posterior, las autoridades colombianas han señalado a la empresaria Zulma Guzmán Castro como presunta responsable, encontrándose actualmente a la espera de su proceso de extradición desde Londres, Reino Unido. No obstante, la nueva línea de investigación solicitada por la familia Graham apunta a evaluar si el propio Juan de Bedout tuvo algún grado de participación o conocimiento en la intoxicación de su esposa en 2021. Por su parte, la defensa del empresario, encabezada por el abogado Fabio Humar, ha manifestado absoluta disposición para colaborar con los requerimientos de la justicia. De acuerdo con fuentes cercanas a la defensa, el propio De Bedout desconoce los fundamentos de esta nueva acusación y sostiene que los análisis toxicológicos realizados en el marco de las investigaciones habrían detectado rastros de talio también en su propio organismo y en el de su hijo mayor, lo que —según esta tesis— los ubicaría a ellos mismos como víctimas de un atentado químico generalizado y no como victimarios. La solicitud formal interpuesta ante la Fiscalía exige que este caso sea asumido por los fiscales especializados que han liderado las pesquisas sobre el talio en el país, con el fin de cruzar la información de los históricos médicos, audios, recetas y órdenes hospitalarias. Mientras las autoridades judiciales evalúan si abren una indagación penal formal por estos hechos del pasado, los desgarradores audios de Alicia Graham vuelven a abrir una herida profunda en una familia golpeada por la tragedia, recordándole al país los peligros invisibles de sustancias letales que operan en la sombra de los círculos más íntimos.

articles.title: Grand Slam of Darts: Jonny Clayton, Ross Smith, Josh Rock, Luke Woodhouse and Beau Greaves all exit tournament
articles.summary: Four seeds were sent crashing out of the tournament on a bumper Sunday while women's star Greaves beat Niels Zonneveld; watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports with the final taking place on Sunday November 22
articles.body:
Fifth seed Clayton was demolished 5-1 in barely 10 minutes by former world champion Rob Cross, who posted an impressive 114 average and finishing stats of 83 per cent.

Clayton was the second seed to be eliminated on Sunday after 15th-seed Luke Woodhouse lost 5-1 to Krzysztof Ratajski.

In the final match of the afternoon session, eighth seed Josh Rock knew he could not afford to lose three legs to Kevin Doets, but he ultimately lost the match 5-3.

And in the evening session, sixth seed Smith beat Gabriel Clemens 5-4, but conceded too many legs and exits the tournament following Saturday's shock loss to Rusty-Jake Rodriguez.

Meanwhile, three-time Women's World Matchplay champion Greaves enjoyed a 5-3 win against Niels Zonneveld, but the scoreline was not enough to keep her in the competition.

Lisa Ashton, Cam Crabtree, Raymond Smith , Adam Sevada, Maik Kuivenhoven, Jan Schmidt , Carl Sneyd and Joe Hunt also had group-stage exits confirmed on Sunday.

Group A: Niels Zonneveld 3-5 Beau Greaves

Beau Greaves recovered from 3-1 down to beat Niels Zonneveld 5-3, but the scoreline was not good enough to see her progress from this year's 'Group of Death'.

Greaves dominated her opponent in the second half of the match, but her 5-2 defeat to Luke Littler on Saturday night sees her once again fail to get out of a group with The Nuke now the hot favourite to progress to the last 16.

Lisa Ashton will need to wait another year for her first win in the Grand Slam of Darts, as she fell to a 5-2 loss to Alan Soutar. That result means whoever wins Monday's clash between Soutar and Jermaine Wattimena will progress.

After losing his opening match to Tommy Morris on Saturday, Premier League star Josh Rock knew he needed to beat Kevin Doets and concede no more than two legs in order to stay in the tournament.

However, Doets posted a 100 average and five 180s as he stormed to a 5-3 victory to eliminate Rock and set up a Monday night showdown with Morris.

Group D: Cameron Menzies 5-4 Raymond Smith

Cameron Menzies fought back from 3-1 down to beat Raymond Smith 5-4 and set up a Monday night decider with Stephen Bunting to see who tops the group.

A spectacular 162 finish in the sixth leg levelled the scores and helped to eliminate the unfortunate Smith, who lost final-leg deciders in both of his matches at the Grand Slam.

Group E: Sebastian Bialecki 5-4 Joe Hunt

Joe Hunt averaged more than 94 and threw a dozen 140s, but was still eliminated from the Grand Slam of Darts in a thrilling 5-4 defeat to Sebastian Bialecki on Sunday evening.

The Polish player edged a last-leg decider to pick up two points and he will now face Gerwyn Price on Monday night to decide who reaches the knockout stage.

Group F: Andrew Gilding 5-4 Charlie Manby

Andrew Gilding averaged just 81, but still found a way to eliminate Charlie Manby from the Grand Slam with a 5-4 victory.

Manby missed his first 12 darts at double in the match before recovering to establish a 3-2 lead, but his opponent won three of the final four legs, ultimately securing the win with a classy 124 checkout on bullseye. He will face Ryan Searle on Monday to decide who progresses.

Jonny Clayton won the opening leg of his must-win clash against Rob Cross, but didn't attempt another double as he was knocked out of the tournament in brutal fashion.

Cross reeled off five legs in a row, including finishes of 138 and 137 in a ruthless performance and will look to take that form into his group decider with Anton Ostlund on Monday.

Niko Springer managed TWO Robin Hoods (where a dart lands in the flight of a previous dart and scores no points) but still cruised to a 5-1 win over Adam Sevada.

That means the winner of Springer's clash with Wessel Nijman on Monday night will reach the last 16.

Joe Cullen suffered a surprise defeat to Paolo Nebrida who kept his hopes of qualification alive with a 5-2 victory.

In a game of poor-quality finishing, the players missed 30 darts at a double between them in seven legs, and while Luke Humphries is now a heavy favourite to progress from Group I, all three players can still technically qualify.

Group J: Luke Woodhouse 1-5 Krzysztof Ratajski

World No 17 Luke Woodhouse became one of the biggest casualties of the tournament so far as he lost five legs in a row in a 5-1 defeat to Krzysztof Ratajski.

That makes it two defeats in two games for 'Woody', while Ratajski will take on Tom Sykes on Tuesday night to decide who makes it into the next round.

After losing 5-1 to James Wade on Saturday, Cam Crabtree needed to avoid losing two legs against Ricky Evans on Sunday to stay in the competition.

The pair served up a quickfire contest to the Wolverhampton crowd and Crabtree missed two match darts, but was ultimately knocked out by Evans who will now face Wade to decide the group.

Group L: Jeffrey de Graaf 4-5 Henry Coates

Henry Coates took Michael van Gerwen to a last-leg decider on Saturday night and the 20-year-old was involved in another thriller on Sunday as he beat Jeffrey de Graaf 5-4.

The result means all three players could still technically qualify from the group.

Carl Sneyd's tournament was ended by an impressive display from Bradley Brooks, who threw five 180s and averaged more than 97 in a 5-3 win.

Brooks will now take on third seed Gian van Veen on Tuesday night, seeking an upset victory to make his way into the second round.

Group N: Martin Schindler 5-0 Jan Schmidt

Martin Schindler whitewashed Jan Schmidt 5-0 in the opening match of the evening session to eliminate his fellow German from the tournament.

Both players struggled on their doubles, but Schindler is the only player who hasn't lost a leg and can now focus on Tuesday's winner-takes-all clash with Chris Dobey to decide who tops the group.

Ross Smith was one of the favourites to win the Grand Slam of Darts, but exits at the group stage despite a gutsy win over Gabriel Clemens.

The European champion needed to win 5-3 or better to keep his tournament hopes alive, but a checkout ratio of less than 19 per cent proved his undoing.

Group P: Karel Sedlacek 4-5 Maik Kuivenhoven

Maik Kuivenhoven was eliminated from the tournament but still recovered from 4-1 down to beat Karel Sedlacek 5-4.

That leaves Sedlacek needing a big win over Nathan Aspinall on Tuesday night to qualify.

articles.title: Russia barred from Junior Ice Hockey World Championships in Canada
articles.summary: Canada says it will not allow Russian athletes to compete in the Junior Ice Hockey World Championships because of the war in Ukraine.
articles.body:
Russia's hopes of reintegration into international sport suffered a setback when it was barred from the upcoming Junior Ice Hockey World Championships.

Canada said it would deny entry to Russian athletes as a result of the war in Ukraine.

"Due to the position and restrictions formally communicated by the Canadian government, the Russian Under-20 national team is unable to participate in the World Junior Championship," the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) said in a statement.

It said that "after carefully assessing the feasibility of alternative arrangements, the IIHF Council has determined that Canada will remain as host and the tournament will proceed from 26 December 2026 to 5 January 2027 in Edmonton and Red Deer."

The Russian Ice Hockey Federation called the IIHF's decision "unacceptable and unlawful" and said it would appeal to the International Olympic Committee (IOC).

"The IIHF's decision was made solely due to political reasons," it said in a statement.

"The exclusion of the Russian national team violates fundamental legal principles, Olympism, the principle of non-discrimination, equality among athletes and the integrity of international tournaments."

Russia had been suspended from competing in IIHF events since the country invaded Ukraine in 2022, but last month the Court of Arbitration for Sport overturned the ban.

It said that the IIHF's arguments citing safety and security were "not supported by sufficient evidence" and ordered it to allow Russia to participate in its events.

The move was welcomed by Russia but condemned by Ukraine and along with some sponsors of the Junior World Championships.

Six European ice hockey federations said they would refuse to play Russia if they were allowed to take part, appearing to leave the tournament in limbo.

On Wednesday the Canadian government said it would deny visas to any Russian athletes, effectively barring them from participating.

It is the latest example of a wider backlash against efforts to allow Russia to return to international sport.

This week Norway, Finland and Estonia said they would block visas for Russian and Belarusian athletes.

Norway is preparing to host skiing's Cross-country World Cup next month, while Finland is due to stage the Figure Skating World Championships in March.

The International Skating Union (ISU) has said it "believes that athletes should not be punished for the actions of their governments in a world where, sadly, many conflicts are ongoing", and that it was "seeking clarifications" from officials in Finland.

In March several athletes from Russia and Belarus were allowed to compete under their national flags at the Winter Paralympics after partial suspensions by the International Paralympic Committee were lifted.

In July the IOC provisionally reinstated Russia to its competitions, saying a ban introduced in 2023 was "no longer applicable".

However, sports federations can enforce their own eligibility criteria.

While World Gymnastics, World Aquatics and World Boxing have removed restrictions on Russian athletes competing, a total ban has been maintained by World Athletics.

Last month it was announced that Moscow will host the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships, the first time an Olympic federation has chosen to stage a global event in Russia since the invasion of Ukraine.

articles.title: How did Serena and Venus Williams turn their first $525,000 home into a nearly $1.8 million profit? Inside the sisters' smart Florida property deal
articles.summary: Serena Williams and Venus Williams made an early real estate investment that brought them a major increase in the property’s value.
articles.body: Serena Williams and Venus Williams made an early real estate investment that brought them a major increase in the property’s value. The sisters bought a one-acre plot in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, for $525,000 in 1998 and built an 8,489-square-foot mansion on it. Nearly two decades later, they sold the property for $2.3 million after initially asking for $2.695 million. The sale brought in $1.775 million more than their original purchase price, before construction costs, taxes and other expenses. It was one of their first major investments outside tennis.How did Serena Williams and Venus Williams make their first property purchase?The sisters were still building their tennis careers when they decided to invest in real estate. Venus Williams turned professional in 1994, followed by Serena Williams in 1995. Both were making progress on the court, and by 1998, they had already started earning money through their careers.That same year, they decided to buy property together. They chose a one-acre plot in the BallenIsles Country Club community in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, and paid $525,000 for it. Instead of purchasing a ready-made house, the sisters wanted to build a home that matched their needs and personal choices.According to Architectural Digest, the project took around two years to complete. The sisters worked on the design and construction before moving into their new home in 2000.The decision also gave them a place where they could spend time together without the demands of their tennis schedules taking over their lives. Both were spending much of the year travelling for tournaments, so having a shared home in Florida gave them a place to return to between competitions.What made Serena Williams and Venus Williams’ mansion special?The completed house covered 8,489 square feet and had six bedrooms. One of its notable features was that both sisters had their own primary suites. This allowed them to enjoy their privacy while continuing to share the property.The interiors had white marble fittings and hardwood floors. Large glass walls brought natural light into the rooms, while the main floor offered plenty of space for relaxing and spending time with guests. There were several lounge areas, a home theatre and specially made trophy cases to display their tennis achievements.The mansion also included a gym, which was a useful addition for two professional athletes who spent much of their time training and preparing for tournaments.The outdoor space was just as impressive. The property had a 5,000-square-foot terraced backyard with a swimming pool, spa and gazebo. It also featured a private artificial lake, adding another feature to the large estate.Architectural Digest and Realtor.com have reported on the property’s design and features. The house gave the sisters plenty of room to live comfortably, train and enjoy time away from their busy tennis careers.Why did Serena Williams and Venus Williams sell their $2.3 million mansion?As the sisters’ careers and personal lives developed, they eventually moved towards having separate homes. Serena began building her own real estate portfolio, while Venus continued with her own property interests.In late 2018, the sisters decided to put their shared Palm Beach Gardens mansion on the market. They initially listed it for $2.695 million. However, the final sale price was lower than their asking price.The property was eventually sold for $2.3 million in early 2019. Architectural Digest reported the original listing and sale details, while Mansion Global also covered the transaction.The numbers show how much the property’s value had changed. The sisters had paid $525,000 for the land in 1998 and received $2.3 million when they sold the completed property. That left a difference of $1.775 million between the original purchase price and the final sale price.The sisters had spent money building the mansion and maintaining it over the years. Taxes, selling costs and other expenses would also affect the final amount they earned.Even with those costs, the sale marked a considerable increase over their original investment.What other properties has Serena Williams bought over the years?The Palm Beach Gardens mansion was only the beginning of Serena’s interest in real estate. She went on to purchase homes in several locations, including Florida and California.In May 2015, Serena bought another five-bedroom home in Palm Beach Gardens for approximately $2.5 million. According to Mansion Global, she later sold the property off-market in late 2020 for around $2.775 million.She also owned a Bel Air estate in California, which she purchased in 2006. In 2017, she and her husband, Alexis Ohanian, bought a home in Beverly Hills. Over the years, Serena has also been connected to properties in Paris and New York.Another major purchase came in September 2020, when she paid $8 million for a waterfront estate in Jupiter, Florida. The property had previously belonged to former MLB player Yadier Molina and covered 10,433 square feet.However, Serena did not intend to keep the existing house as it was. According to Architectural Digest, she filed a demolition notice in October 2020, just one month after buying the property. She planned to clear the existing structure and develop a custom home on the land.Her more recent Florida residence has also drawn attention. In September 2026, Architectural Digest featured her 14,500-square-foot waterfront mansion north of Miami. Serena purchased the property in 2017 for $5.7 million and later spent three years renovating it. Her sister Venus and her design firm, V Starr, helped with the project.The sisters’ first shared property remains an important part of their real estate history. Their 1998 purchase in Palm Beach Gardens eventually became a $2.3 million sale, showing that their investments outside tennis also became a significant part of their financial journey.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Kansas City Current has punched its ticket to the NWSL championship game.
articles.body:
Kansas City Current has punched its ticket to the NWSL championship game.

Kansas City beat Gotham FC 2-1 on Sunday to advance to the title match, where it will face the Washington Spirit, who downed Utah Royals FC on Saturday in the semifinal.

Kansas City had the edge through the early part of the game. The Current took a 1-0 lead in the 20th minute when Croix Bethune scored on a free kick.

That lead held through the end of the first period and into the second, but Gotham finally answered in the 69th minute. Gotham got the ball into the box on a cross, and Kansas City's Laney Rouse was trying to clear it when she hit it into her own goal.

articles.title: Career Turning Point: How Simone Biles rebuilt her career after Tokyo to become a mental health voice and Olympic legend
articles.summary: Simone Biles went from facing one of the most difficult moments of her sporting career at the 2021 Tokyo Olympics to becoming a leading voice for mental
articles.body: Simone Biles went from facing one of the most difficult moments of her sporting career at the 2021 Tokyo Olympics to becoming a leading voice for mental health in sports. Her decision to withdraw from several events after experiencing the twisties changed how athletes talk about their well-being. It also changed her public image, opening new opportunities beyond gymnastics. Biles returned to win four medals at the 2024 Paris Olympics, taking her career total to 11 Olympic medals and 41 World Championship and Olympic medals combined.Why Did Simone Biles Withdraw From the 2021 Tokyo Olympics?Before the Tokyo Games, Simone Biles was already one of the most successful gymnasts in history. She had won four gold medals and one bronze at the 2016 Rio Olympics. She had also introduced difficult routines that became known by her name, including the Biles on floor exercise and the Yurchenko double pike vault.Expectations were high when she arrived in Tokyo in July 2021. But the competition took a sudden turn during the women’s team final. While attempting an Amanar vault, which requires two and a half twists, Biles lost her sense of direction in the air. She completed only one and a half twists before landing awkwardly.The problem was known as the “twisties”. It happens when gymnasts lose their sense of position while performing in the air. They may struggle to understand where their bodies are or how much they are rotating. At the speed and height involved in elite gymnastics, this can lead to serious injuries.Biles decided to withdraw from the team final and later pulled out of the individual all-around, vault, uneven bars and floor exercise finals. She did not want to risk an accident by competing when she could not safely control her movements.There was also more happening behind the scenes. Biles was dealing with the lasting effects of the abuse committed by former USA Gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar. She was among the survivors who continued to speak about the failures that allowed the abuse to happen. The pandemic-delayed Games added another layer of pressure.How Did Simone Biles Turn the Tokyo Setback Into a Mental Health Movement?Biles’ decision did not receive universal support at first. Some critics questioned why an athlete at the peak of her career would walk away from an Olympic final. Others struggled to understand the seriousness of the twisties. But her explanation helped people see that the problem was not about losing confidence or giving up. It was about being unable to perform safely.She remained with her teammates, cheering them on as the United States won silver in the team event. On August 3, 2021, she returned for the balance beam final. Rather than attempting her usual difficult dismount, she changed it to a safer double pike. She finished with a bronze medal, giving her a second medal from the Tokyo Games.Her decision also brought attention to the mental health pressures faced by athletes who are expected to perform at their best regardless of what they are experiencing personally.The following month, Biles appeared before the US Senate Judiciary Committee on September 15, 2021, to speak about the FBI’s handling of the Larry Nassar investigation. She joined fellow survivors McKayla Maroney, Maggie Nichols and Aly Raisman in asking officials to take responsibility for the failures that allowed Nassar to abuse athletes.Her appearance showed that her concerns went beyond her own career. She wanted better protection for young gymnasts and other athletes who could face similar situations. The hearing also gave her a larger platform to speak about athlete safety and accountability.How Did Simone Biles Build Her Brand Beyond Gymnastics?Biles’ growing public presence also changed the way brands viewed her. Before Tokyo, much of her public image was built around medals, difficult routines and competition results. After the Games, her openness about mental health became another important part of her identity.One of the biggest changes had already happened in April 2021, when she ended her nearly six-year partnership with Nike and signed a long-term deal with Athleta, the activewear brand owned by Gap Inc.The agreement gave Biles an opportunity to work on her own clothing collections and projects aimed at young girls. It was also a partnership that focused on women’s empowerment and the issues she wanted to discuss outside gymnastics.When she withdrew from the Tokyo team final, Athleta publicly supported her. The company said it stood by her well-being both in and out of competition. Visa also backed her decision, showing that her sponsors were not turning away because she had stepped out of the competition.Her commercial profile continued to grow in the following years. In 2022, she appeared on her first Wheaties cereal box as part of the brand’s 100th anniversary celebrations. She received another limited-edition box in January 2023, this time highlighting her adoption story and support for children in foster care.Her work with Friends of the Children also gave her a platform to support young people who need long-term guidance and mentorship. These partnerships showed that her influence was no longer limited to gymnastics fans.Her social media presence also became an important part of that connection. Biles shared more of her life outside competitions, including her training, recovery, family life and experiences with fellow athletes.Her Instagram audience, which stood at around 3.9 million in April 2021, later grew to more than 11 million. This gave her a direct way to connect with people who followed her for reasons beyond her sporting achievements.How Did Simone Biles Complete Her Comeback at the 2024 Paris Olympics?After stepping away from gymnastics following Tokyo, Biles returned to competition in 2023. Her comeback was closely followed because many wanted to see how she would perform after such a difficult Olympic experience.She made her return to the World Championships in Antwerp, Belgium, where she won four gold medals and one silver. The results showed that she could still compete at the highest level.At 27, Biles arrived at the 2024 Paris Olympics for her third Games. She helped the United States win gold in the women’s team final before claiming another gold in the individual all-around competition. She then won the vault final and finished second in the floor exercise.That gave her four medals in Paris, taking her Olympic total to 11, including seven gold, two silver and two bronze medals. She also reached 41 medals across the Olympic Games and World Championships, making her the most decorated gymnast in the sport’s history, according to USA Gymnastics.Her Paris performance was important for another reason. It showed that her decision to step away in Tokyo had not ended her career. She had returned when she was ready, competed on her own terms and added four more Olympic medals to her record.The Tokyo Games remain a major part of Biles’ story, but they are no longer defined only by her withdrawal. Her journey since then has connected elite sport with conversations about mental health, athlete safety, sponsorships and the responsibilities that come with a public platform.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: The full Division III football bracket, along with at least 1 major snub
articles.summary: It's great news for Wisconsin-Whitewater's quest to return to its 2010s glory. Or if you're a New England school.
articles.body:
The transition from a selection committee to the NCAA Power Index (NPI) has taken some of the guess work from the Division III football championship bracket. The expansion from 32 teams to 40 has ensured fewer snubs.

But that doesn't mean this year's field doesn't bring surprises. Geographic limitations and the NPI's difference of opinion with the D3Football.com rankings means there's plenty to quibble about with this year's schedule. Wheaton College, the first team to beat powerhouse North Central in the regular season since 2019, went from the poll's No. 1 team to the bracket's third overall seed. Wisconsin-Whitewater, chasing its first national title since 2014, will have home field advantage all the way to the national championship game in Salem, Virginia after topping out the NPI formula.

Teams with solid resumes, like Bethel and reigning national champion Wisconsin-River Falls, were left out. The New England Small College Athletic Conference (NESCAC) put three teams in the bracket even though the league didn't play a single out-of-conference game . North Central and DePauw, each ranked in the poll's top 15, will face off in a second round game that ensures at least one realistic title contender will be gone before the field is whittled down to 16 teams.

You can find the full bracket here . Or expand the image below.

The tournament begins November 21. The national title will be decided, on January 3, on ESPN.

Glad you asked! DePauw at North Central is the obvious call. But that only gives way to a slate of third round bangers. We could get another Mary Hardin-Baylor vs. Whitewater matchup, a test of Calvin's mettle against Wisconsin-Platteville and Saint John's against whomever wins that DePauw/North Central showdown.

The Timberwolves will be without one of their defensive spark plugs for multiple weeks, the name announced Sunday.

Jaylen Clark left Saturday's loss to Chicago after just three minutes of playing time due to hamstring soreness. An MRI conducted revealed a right hamstring strain.

The Timberwolves said Clark will be re-evaluated in two weeks.

Clark has been a regular rotational fixture in recent weeks, with Minnesota utilizing his perimeter defense and general energy in a multitude of ways.

The Wolves' wing depth will continue to be tested moving forward without Clark, Anthony Edwards nor Donte DiVincenzo available for the foreseeable future.

articles.title: Chiefs thrash Falcons as Mahomes throws five touchdowns
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes threw for five touchdowns and 348 yards as the Kansas City Chiefs thrashed the Falcons 35-13 at Atlanta on Sunday.Cyrus Allen and Andrew Arms...
articles.body:
Patrick Mahomes threw for five touchdowns and 348 yards as the Kansas City Chiefs thrashed the Falcons 35-13 at Atlanta on Sunday.

Mahomes was back to his imperious best, completing 22-of-35 passes with zero interceptions and one sack in a win that took the Chiefs level with the idle Denver Broncos top of the AFC West.

Rookie Emmett Johnson twice found the end zone, while Josh Downs had a touchdown on his Kansas City debut following a deadline day trade from Indianapolis.

Cyrus Allen and Andrew Armstrong each scored their first Chiefs touchdowns, grabbing passes of 39 yards and 43 yards respectively as Mahomes dominated the Falcons defense.

It was the three-time Super Bowl champion quarterback's most impressive showing since his nine-month injury absence after tearing his knee ligaments last December.

"Guys made plays, you know? I gave them chances downfield, and they went out there and made plays happen," said Mahomes.

Johnson -- stepping up for Kenneth Walker III, who was absent with a groin injury -- also led the Chiefs' running game, with 22 carries for 101 yards.

Star tight end Travis Kelce left the field early, injuring his ankle as he was tackled taking his first catch, but returned in the second quarter.

"I thought we did a great job picking up, obviously Kenneth not being here. I thought Emmett did a great job, and then the O-line gave me chances to throw the ball down the field," said Mahomes.

It was another miserable day for the Falcons, who trailed 28-3 before Bijan Robinson's fourth-quarter touchdown, and have now lost three straight and five of their past six.

Elsewhere, the Cleveland Browns rallied from 17-0 down to stun the Houston Texans 27-24, as Quinshon Judkins ran in a touchdown with less than a minute remaining.

The Texans had led with C.J. Stroud's first-half passing touchdowns to Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson.

The Browns fought back to take the lead with touchdowns either side of halftime, from a Deshaun Watson six-yard run, a KC Concepcion rushing touchdown and two field goals, all without reply.

The Texans thought they had salvaged the win with a Stroud pass to Dalton Schultz, before Watson led yet another late game-winning drive and Judkins ran five yards for the win with 53 seconds left.

"It was definitely a big win for us overall, but personally for me it was definitely special," said Watson, who was drafted by the Texans in 2017 and traded to Cleveland five years later.

Kirk Cousins threw for two touchdowns even as he was sacked three times on his return to the Minnesota Vikings, who beat divisional rivals Green Bay 30-10 on Sunday.

Despite having just a few days to adjust to his new team, Cousins sent a 38-yard pass to Myles Price in the first quarter, and sealed victory with a 20-yard pass to tight end Gavin Bartholomew in the fourth.

Cousins spent six successful seasons with the Vikings between 2018 and 2023, but tore his Achilles tendon at the Packers' Lambeau Field and subsequently had spells with the Falcons and the Las Vegas Raiders before returning to Minnesota last week.

"It was emotional, coming to the stadium three years ago, tearing my Achilles here, and it's been a tough three years," said Cousins.

"It's been a tough three years and there's more of the story being written."

The Detroit Lions thrashed New England 35-10 in Munich, Germany, after the Patriots' quarterback Drake Maye left the field with an ankle injury following a sack from behind by Aidan Hutchinson in the first quarter.

Lions defensive end Hutchinson then suffered a knee injury celebrating the sack.

The Carolina Panthers needed a field goal with two seconds remaining to beat their divisional rival New Orleans Saints and move top of the NFC South.

articles.title: Takeaways from Miami Dolphins' 24-22 loss vs. Indianapolis Colts
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins fell just short of a victory on the road against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 10. Here's what we took away from the loss.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins are now 1-8 after a narrow 24-22 loss to the Indianapolis Colts in Week 10.

The Dolphins were without starting quarterback Malik Willis, who was placed on injured reserve with a groin injury he had been dealing with. Backup Kyle McCord unfortunately didn't prove to be a winning answer for Miami.

This was a game the Dolphins could have feasibly won since the Colts came in at 2-7 and have been trading away multiple key players for future assets. The Colts traded away two key wide receivers at the deadline, sending Josh Downs to Kansas City and Keenan Allen to San Francisco.

Missed field goals, crucial turnovers and offensive struggles are the ultimate reasons Miami couldn't come away victorious. Here are 5 takeaways from the Dolphins' Week 10 loss to Indianapolis.

Dolphins' kicker Zane Gonzalez missed three kicks in Sunday's game, two field goals and one extra point, costing the Dolphins seven points.

In a two-point loss, it is easy to point out the missed kicks as the primary reason Miami could not come away with the win. Gonzalez is the second kicker the Dolphins have used in 2026, signing him after waiving Riley Patterson following Week 5.

Gonzalez finished the day 1-for-3 on field goals, missing from 51 and 47 yards. On extra points, he was 1-for-2. Gonzalez has now missed kicks in three consecutive games. Considering this is a recurring issue, the Dolphins should move on from Gonzalez immediately.

The young Dolphins secondary shined against a struggling Daniel Jones

The Dolphins defense showed out against the Colts' passing attack, holding quarterback Daniel Jones to just 108 yards passing and two interceptions.

The interceptions were recorded by a pair of rookies, first by safety Michael Taaffe and again by cornerback Chris Johnson, who returned it 59 yards for a touchdown.

This was Taaffe's third interception of the season while also adding six tackles on the day. He continues to prove that he's a steal of the 2026 draft as a fifth-round pick.

Johnson's interception return for touchdown brought the game back to within a single score, cutting the Colts' lead to 21-16 in the third quarter. Johnson now has interceptions in back-to-back games and his first career pick-six. Turning interceptions into touchdowns is something Johnson showed the ability to do at San Diego State, doing it twice last season.

Colts relied on the run game offensively, and it was effective

The Colts were able to generate an efficient offense by sticking to the run game. Jonathan Taylor led the way with 83 yards on 16 attempts. Rookie Seth McGowan also had an impressive day with 77 yards and a touchdown on 12 attempts.

In total, the Colts had 172 yards on the ground and averaged 5.1 yards per carry. The time of possession was just about even, with the Colts just slightly winning the battle. If the Miami defense could have done a better job containing the run, this game could have had a very different result

Except for a few big plays, it was an overall mediocre performance by Kyle McCord. He finished the game completing 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards and a rushing touchdown.

Although McCord didn't throw an interception, he was responsible for a strip-sack that resulted in a Colts touchdown. On the opening play of the third quarter with the Dolphins backed up at their own 10-yard line, Colts' cornerback Justin Walley got to McCord and forced the fumble, which was recovered in the end zone by defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore. This gave the Colts a 21-7 lead.

Later in the third quarter, McCord was able to lead a seven-play, 71-yard touchdown drive in which he completed an impressive 38-yard pass to Caleb Douglas and finished the drive with a rushing touchdown from three yards out. The Dolphins were unfortunately unable to convert a potential game-tying two-point conversion, and the score remained 24-22 at the start of the fourth quarter, the eventual final score. The Dolphins had three more drives to try and take the lead, and they resulted in a missed field goal, a punt and a turnover on downs.

Ultimately, McCord didn't show many signs of being able to turn the Dolphins into a winning football team any more than Malik Willis has.

Chop Robinson added another sack to what is becoming an impressive 2026 campaign

Dolphins edge rusher Chop Robinson recorded his fifth sack of the season today on Jones. Robinson now has four sacks in his last four games and is pressuring opposing quarterbacks consistently.

Robinson finished today's game with five tackles, a sack, and two QB hits. But his box score often doesn't quite illustrate his impact on the game. Robinson came into this game leading the league in pass rush win rate at about 36%.

This is a big year for Robinson in securing a long-term future with the Miami Dolphins , and his play as of late has to be incentivizing the front office to strongly consider offering him an extension when that time comes.

articles.title: Matthew Stafford throws two TD passes, Rams lead Cardinals 17-6 at halftime
articles.summary: The Rams have more injury issues to deal with on offense.
articles.body:
The Rams have more injury issues to deal with on offense. But the club scored two quick touchdowns late in the second quarter to take a 17-6 lead over the Cardinals into halftime.

Matthew Stafford tossed a 5-yard touchdown pass to Tyler Higbee to cap a 10-play, 72-yard drive late in the second quarter.

Then rookie Carson Beck threw a tough-luck interception, as Devin Duvernay dropped a pass that went right to him and defensive back Kam Kinchens came away with the pass — returning it to Arizona's 32-yard line.

A few plays later, Stafford connected with Xavier Smith on a screen for a 22-yard touchdown, putting the Rams up by 11.

With top pass catchers out, Stafford is 15-of-23 for 176 yards with two TDs and one pick.

Blake Corum and Kyren Williams have been on the field together much more than usual. Corum has 46 yards on eight carries while Williams has 9 yards on five carries. He's also caught two passes for 9 yards while Corum has three receptions for 19 yards.

But the Rams lost their top two centers due to injury. Coleman Shelton (hamstring) and backup Dylan McMahon (knee) are both doubtful to return. Guard Beaux Limmer slid over to center with Bill Murray coming in to play left guard.

For the Cardinals, Beck is 8-of-13 for 88 yards with a pick in his first start.

Arizona has just 87 yards, four first downs, and is 0-of-4 on third down.

The Rams will have a chance to add to their lead to start the third quarter, as they'll receive the second-half kickoff.

articles.title: Inside New Chiefs Acquisition Josh Downs’ Debut Vs. Falcons
articles.summary: Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired during the NFL trade deadline, was used early and often vs. the Falcons. He was the main punt returner and caught a touch...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs wasted no time in unwrapping their new toy.

Wide receiver Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired from the Indianapolis Colts for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks on Tuesday, was involved early in Sunday's 35-13 victory at the Atlanta Falcons.

Downs, who had four catches for 51 yards and a touchdown, played in every drive of the first quarter, but it was on special teams where he first saw action.

After the Falcons went three-and-out on the game's opening series, Downs was back to return the punt, though it ended up being a touchback. He was the returner on all three of the Chiefs' punt returns.

In the second quarter, Downs really picked up steam on the offensive side.

On the Chiefs' last drive of the first half, Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker kicked a 41-yard field goal, but the Falcons jumped offside on fourth down, giving the Chiefs a first down and another offensive opportunity.

It turned out to be a costly mistake for the Falcons, which would change the game.

Lined up with two other wide receivers on the left side, Downs ran an option route, which is one of his specialties, and Patrick Mahomes showed faith in him despite double coverage from defensive backs Billy Bowman Jr. and C.J. Henderson. The result was an 18-yard touchdown .

"That's a trust play," Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said.

Two offensive plays before his first touchdown as a Chiefs player, Downs was targeted on consecutive plays, which resulted in a 13-yard catch and then an incompletion.

Downs' lone downside — lame pun intended — came on the Chiefs' second punt return when he fumbled the 50-yard punt, forcing the Chiefs to start their possession on their own four-yard line.

The Chiefs did have some special teams gaffes, including allowing an onside kick to be converted, but Downs was part of a prolific, downfield Chiefs passing game.

Mahomes completed 22-of-35 passes for 348 yards and five touchdowns.

"Pat had a huge day," Reid said, "and was slinging it."

Backup wide receiver Andrew Armstrong scored a 43-yard touchdown on 3rd and 1. Mahomes connected with receiver Rashee Rice who had a 50-yard contested catch for the longest gain of the game.

Rice and Downs have their own connection, having trained together in the offseason and coming out of college.

The Chiefs knew they were getting a dog in Downs after seeing him lead the Colts with seven catches for 72 yards during the Colts' overtime loss to Kansas City in Week Two.

"We saw that firsthand," Reid said. "I had to watch him live, which wasn't good."

Further confirmation came from conversations with Chris Ballard, who the Colts fired as general manager earlier this year. Prior to his tenure in Indianapolis, Ballard worked in the Chiefs personnel department from 2013 to 2016.

"Ballard," Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy said, "spoke rave reviews about the kid."

Ballard and the Colts signed Downs to his rookie, four-year $5.52 million contract, which expires after 2026 season.

The Chiefs will have to determine whether to re-sign Downs after the season.

But that's a story for a day in the future.

In the present he's already helping the Chiefs.

"Our new guy, Downs," Reid said, "it looks like there's a connection there."

articles.title: Good, bad and ugly coming out of Packers' Week 10 loss to Vikings
articles.summary: Highlighting the good, the bad and the ugly coming out of the Packers' 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers fumbled on the offense's second play, trailed 3-0 early and 17-0 at halftime and lost 30-10 to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday at Lambeau Field. The visitors dominated an important midseason NFC North showdown, tallying four takeaways and eight sacks against a hapless Packers offense and handing Matt LaFleur's team a third division loss in four games.

Highlighting the good, the bad and the ugly coming out of Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings:

The adversity defense: The Packers turned the ball over at their own 10-yard line (Mark Redman fumble), own 27-yard line (John Williams snap) and their own 35-yard line (J. Michael Sturdivant fumble) and had one other giveaway in Vikings territory, but Minnesota managed only nine points off turnovers. The defense did its best to keep the Packers in the game despite the offense and special teams giving the ball away four times. The Packers could have easily been down 7-0 immediately after Redman fumbled the ball away on the offense's second play, but Barryn Sorrell's sack all but ended the drive. Lukas Van Ness also had a sack to force a field goal following a giveaway.

Third-and-long defense: The Packers allowed a 38-yard touchdown pass on 3rd-and-23, a 24-yard pass on 3rd-and-15 (setting up a touchdown) and a 16-yard pass on a 3rd-and-12 (setting up a touchdown). Had the Packers simply made those stops on third down and forced the Vikings to either kick field goals or punt, they could have prevented as many as 15 points. Losing in favorable down-and-distances killed the Packers defense, which generally played well down to down (allowed only 4.8 yards per play). Credit to Kirk Cousins for creating game-changing plays on third down.

The offensive line implodes again: Another new starting offensive line combination got run over by Brian Flores in the Vikings. The Packers allowed eight sacks and 12 quarterback hits, and the run game produced only 56 rushing yards and a 3.3-yard average. The Vikings stress an offensive line better than any defense in football, but the collective performance from Jordan Morgan, Laken Tomlinson, John Williams, Travis Glover and Anthony Belton simply wasn't good enough. Minnesota got free runners at the quarterback, consistently confused blockers with twists and stunts and consistently won 1-on-1 matchups. Williams botched a simple shotgun snap. The Packers have navigated the offensive line issues over the last two months, but Sunday was a stark reminder of the lingering issues up front. Per ESPN, Jordan Love was under pressure on 60 percent of his dropbacks. What quarterback can operate when pressured 21 times in a game?

articles.title: Game balls from the Saints' woeful loss to the Panthers
articles.summary: There weren't many positives to take away from yet another New Orleans Saints home loss, but there were a couple of standouts to highlight.
articles.body:
Another Sunday and another loss for the New Orleans Saints at home. This time, it was a 20-17 last-second defeat to the Carolina Panthers . The defeat dropped the Saints to 3-6 overall and a laughable 1-3 in the Superdome while giving control of the equally laughable NFC South to Carolina.

New Orleans played well defensively through most of the game. Like in previous weeks though, late defensive breakdowns would put the game in doubt. This time, however, those failures cost New Orleans the game with a 54-yard game-winning field goal from Ryan Fitzgerald on the games final play. The Saints offense didn't help their own cause with their failure to run the football and protect quarterback Tyler Shough (again!) while mixing in a couple costly turnovers and hurting themselves. It feels like we're reaching, but here were the best performers of another woeful effort.

If not for Fitzgerald's game-winner, Charlie Smyth would likely get some accolades. Down 17-14 with 1:43 left, Shough drove the Saints 41 yards in 8 plays, aided by a Carolina penalty, into long field goal range. The conservative play-calling at the end of the drive was an interesting decision, since New Orleans had missed five of eight field goal tries from beyond 50 yards this season. Nevertheless, Smyth lined up for a 55-yard try with less than 40 seconds left. He'd nail the field goal, the second longest of his career, to give New Orleans a short-lived tie.

Most expected the rookie first round pick, the eighth overall selection, to continue to get somewhat limited reps in his second game back from a hamstring injury. Instead, Tyson caught 11 passes for 80 yards to lead both teams in receiving. On a day when Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele, and Juwan Johnson were all contained with a combined 7 catches and 72 yards, Tyson came through in a big way. The Saints got their rookie involved heavily, as he showed impressive chemistry with Shough. Tyson was targeted 13 times, making several acrobatic grabs on intermediate routes and impressive agility after short throws. The Saints clearly don't have much, but Tyson's addition to a crew that includes Olave, Vele, and Johnson should be fun to watch down the stretch.

articles.title: Tessa Johnson breaks A’ja Wilson record in South Carolina’s thrilling win over JuJu Watkins, USC
articles.summary: Tessa Johnson scored a career-high 28 points Sunday, surpassing a South Carolina women’s basketball scoring record held by A’ja Wilson as the top-ranked Game...
articles.body:
Tessa Johnson scored a career-high 28 points Sunday, surpassing a South Carolina women's basketball scoring record held by A'ja Wilson as the top-ranked Gamecocks defeated No. 3 USC 89-85 on Sunday at Bon Secours Wellness Arena.

According to ESPN Insights, Johnson's total was the highest by a South Carolina player against an Associated Press top-five opponent in the past 25 seasons. Wilson previously held that mark with 27 points against UConn in the 2018 Elite Eight.

Johnson also made two free throws with 13 seconds remaining to give South Carolina a four-point lead after Jordan Lee's block on JuJu Watkins helped stop USC's comeback. The Gamecocks improved to 4-0, while the Trojans fell to 3-1. According to Steve Reed of The Associated Press, prior to Sunday's matchup against the Gamecocks, USC had surpassed 100 points in each of its first three games.

Johnson scored or assisted on 34 points, according to ESPN Insights. She made six of 10 contested shots and went 5-for-8 in the paint.

Her first-half shooting helped South Carolina recover from an early deficit. Johnson scored 17 points before halftime, making six of seven field-goal attempts, including all three of her 3-point tries. The Gamecocks used a 9-0 run to take a 49-45 halftime lead and did not trail again.

USC cut a 12-point deficit with less than four minutes remaining to two with 42 seconds left, getting 3-pointers from Jazzy Davidson and Watkins during the rally.

Following a South Carolina turnover, Lee blocked Watkins on a fast-break drive. Officials initially ruled the ball went out of bounds off Lee. After USC called timeout, South Carolina coach Dawn Staley challenged the ruling. The call was overturned, giving the Gamecocks possession with 15 seconds remaining.

USC then fouled Johnson, who made both attempts.

Joyce Edwards finished with 20 points and 10 rebounds for South Carolina. Chloe Kitts added 15 points and 12 rebounds for her third consecutive double-double. The Gamecocks shot 55% from the field and held USC to 42%.

Watkins led the Trojans with 25 points on 8-for-12 shooting. Saniyah Hall contributed 17 points and nine rebounds, while Kennedy Smith scored 15.

Per The Associated Press, South Carolina will host Florida Gulf Coast in its home opener Tuesday. The Trojans return home to face Baylor on Friday night.
