articles.title: Recap: Deshaun Watson strikes late against Texans, secures Bowns' comeback win
articles.summary: The Houston Texans had the win. Untlil the defense stepped up on the field for the final drive in the fourth quater. How many times have fans heard that sent...
articles.body:
Untlil the defense stepped up on the field for the final drive in the fourth quater.

How many times have fans heard that sentiment before, knowing heartbreak would follow as soon as the team exited the field?

Well, Sunday's was different because of who was on the other side securing the comeback.

Former Texans quarterback Deshaun Watson guided a comeback drive for the Cleveland Browns , setting up the game-winning Quinshon Judkins 5-yard touchdown run with 53 seconds remaining, securing the Browns a 27-24 win at home.

Cleveland (6-4) ended a two-game skid by rallying from an early 17-point deficit behind a strong second half from Watson, who now moves to 2-0 against his former team since being traded in 2022.

Watson, a forme first-round pick in 2017 by Houston, threw for 312 yards and rushed for 50 yards — including a 6-yard touchdown run following a massive 46-yard pass to Jerry Jeudy in the first half. Wth the scoring drive in the final minute of action, Watson picked up his sixth game-winning moment this season.

But it didn't have to be this way for Houston. Quarterback C.J. Stroud and the Texans offense looked red hot out of the gate, taking a 17-0 first-quarter lead behind two touchdown throws from the potential MVP-caliber passer. The Texans defense also held Cleveland's offense to 22 yards in the first quarter and zero first down.

But as the game continued, momentum moved in favor of the Browns. Watson helped set up a field goal from Andre Szmyt to make it a one-possession game before halftime. Stroud, who finished with 211 passing yards and three touchdowns, tossed an interception to Tyson Campbell with less than two minutes remaining in the second quarter.

Houston's offense did nothing in the third quarter, allowing the Browns to tie the game at 17 after a 6-yard touchdown run by rookie K.C. Concepcion. Stroud and the offense had fourth straight three-and-out drives before eventually getting something moving back in their favor.

As the fourth quarter wound down, the Texans were still in position to pull it out. After a pass interference call against the Browns, Stroud hit Dalton Schultz for an 11-yard touchdown with just over nine minutes left on the clock. Cleveland's next two drives ended with a punt and a pick by Watson, giving Houston a chance to close the door.

The Texans return to Reliant Stadium on Thursday for a matchup against the Indianapolis Colts. Houston will look to pick up its first win at home in 2026.

articles.title: Talaysia Cooper helps No. 21 Mississippi women defeat Louisiana Tech 69-53
articles.summary: (AP) — Talaysia Cooper scored 13 points and No. 21 Mississippi never trailed in a 69-53 victory over Louisiana Tech on Sunday.
articles.body:
OXFORD, Miss. (AP) — Talaysia Cooper scored 13 points and No. 21 Mississippi never trailed in a 69-53 victory over Louisiana Tech on Sunday.

Cooper made 1 of 6 shots from outside the 3-point line and 5 of 9 inside it for the Rebels (4-0). Rachael Okokoh added eight points and six rebounds off the bench, while Desrae Kyles grabbed 10 rebounds.

Jada Richard scored all nine of her points in the first half and Ole Miss turned a 21-12 first-quarter lead into a 40-18 advantage at halftime.

The two teams battled to a 16-all third quarter before seven players scored for the Lady Techsters (4-1) in winning the fourth 19-13.

Kaleigh Thompson and Alexia Weaver both scored 10 to lead Louisiana Tech.

Ole Miss, which has yet to play away from home, shot 48% overall but only 28% from distance — 5 for 18. The Rebels missed 6 of 10 free throws.

Louisiana Tech shot 39% and missed 10 of 13 from 3-point range. The Lady Techsters sank 10 of 15 foul shots.

The Rebels won the rebound battle 45-25 with 20 coming at the offensive end, leading to 24 second-chance points.

Louisiana Tech scored 23 points off 23 turnovers by the Rebels. Ole Miss scored 15 off 24 forced turnovers.

Louisiana Tech hosts Arkansas-Pine Bluff on Wednesday.

Mississippi plays at No. 17 Ohio State on Wednesday.

articles.title: Topps reveals Gem Mint 10 Lando Norris card with Coca-Cola suit patch
articles.summary: The signed 2024 Dynasty card features two race suit relics beneath Norris’s autograph
articles.body:
Topps has shared one of its rarest Lando Norris cards: a signed 2024 Dynasty Formula 1 card with two pieces of race suit, one of them cut from the Coca-Cola logo on the sleeve of his McLaren race suit.

The Topps Racing account posted a short video of the card on Instagram on Friday, with the caption "This Lando Norris patch auto goes CRAZY!"

The card comes from the Single Driver Dual Relic Autograph set. Two windows of red fabric sit below Norris's signature. The left-hand piece shows part of the white Coca-Cola script.

It has been graded by the American company PSA, which sealed it in a plastic case with its highest grade, Gem Mint 10.

Fans spotted the logo straight away. "Where did they get his race suit?" asked one of the commenters under the post. "Omg this is so dope," someone else commented, while another added: "Hahaha Coca-Cola wants to come back to Spain and see the chaos that erupted over the Coca-Cola bottle. Coca-Cola, become a sponsor of LN4 Fusion!"

Norris went viral after the Spanish Grand Prix at the new Madring Circuit during a moment in the cooldown room. Norris was seemingly asked to put down the Coca-Cola he was drinking, but he refused. "I just did a race, so I'm allowed to drink what I would like. Thank you so much," Norris said at the time.

The moment caused chaos online as PepsiCo, a rival of Coca-Cola, is an official partner of F1.

Norris was pressed further on the situation while speaking to the media in Austin, Texas. "No, no one's ever said anything to me since. I feel like we should be allowed to drink whatever we want after a race, especially when you're in it for two hours.

"It's been some of the hottest races, cars are also difficult to drive, so I feel like I should be allowed to drink what I want."

He added: "From a team, the team might have been told off more than I was. And therefore we have little holders to put our drinks in, so it's unbranded, but I'm allowed to drink whatever I can. It's just the branding issues that they have.

"But this is not something I need to be thinking of, or I should be thinking of, so it's some stuff I'm sure that was cleared up between other people. That's simply all it was I think. It's just TV and branding and all of those things, but I can drink whatever I like."

Dynasty is the most expensive F1 product Topps makes. Each box holds a single encased card, always an autograph with a relic, and every one is numbered to 10 copies or fewer. When the 2024 edition went on sale in February 2025, a box cost $1,099.99 .

The base version of this Norris card is limited to 10 copies, with rarer red, black and gold versions on top.

To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

articles.title: Smyth scores 55-yard field goal in Saints defeat
articles.summary: Kicker Charlie Smyth lands a late 55-yard field goal but it is not enough to stop New Orleans Saints falling to a 20-17 defeat against Carolina Panthers on S...
articles.body:
Kicker Charlie Smyth landed a late 55-yard field goal, but it was not enough to stop the New Orleans Saints falling to a 20-17 defeat against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.

The former Gaelic footballer, from Mayobridge in County Down, was making his second NFL appearance of the season after being elevated from the practice squad for a second successive week.

The 25-year-old helped the Saints to an overtime win against Cleveland Browns last weekend with three field goals and two extra points and he was almost the hero again against the Panthers.

Smyth, who also kicked two extra points, landed a 55-yard field goal with just 41 seconds left in regulation time to tie the game at 17-17.

However, Panthers quarterback Bryce Young's drive set up kicker Ryan Fitzgerald to score a 54-yard field goal on the final play to win the game.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 10 RB Report: Travis Etienne Jr. returns for Saints while Seth McGowan cuts into JT's usage again
articles.summary: We over some key backfield splits from Week 10, and what it means for fantasy football going forward.
articles.body:
The early window on Sunday usually gives us a handful of backfields to cover when it comes to the RB usage split. This week, however, there wasn't so much there. Many teams rode one back to glory (or failure) in Week 10, plus a lot of backfields are looking pretty lackluster for fantasy managers (we're looking at you, Cleveland and Houston).

But with the injury carousel still spinning and the trade deadline in the rearview mirror for Jonathan Taylor and the Colts, we have some storylines to discuss in the RB report. We're going to tackle a few notable backfield splits from the Sunday slate and what it means going forward for fantasy managers.

What a gross game this turned out to be. We thought that Saints-Panthers might present some sneaky-good opportunities for fantasy given the point total had moved up to 48.5 prior to kickoff. This was not the case as the teams went well under, combining for 37 points in a 20-17 win for Carolina. Anyway, let's check in on the Saints backfield with Travis Etienne Jr. coming off IR …

… it was just as gross as the offense overall.

Etienne led the way in carries and was tied with Kamara for receptions, but the veteran was the one who scored each of NOLA's touchdowns — one a three-yard rush, the other a five-yard pass. Despite shelling out the money for Etienne this offseason and Kamara aging, the Saints felt the need to continue to rotate backs (at least for this week). Even in the second half, Estimé was getting carries here and there, while Kamara mixed in on passing downs and in the red zone.

Maybe Estimé's presence was merely to keep Etienne's workload down in his return from a hamstring injury, an ailment that can be tricky. But Kamara was also heavily used throughout the contest. You'd think once Etienne is back up to speed, it'll go back to being a two-headed dragon of sorts (though this run game isn't imposing at all).

The Saints get the Bears in Week 11, an offense that should push New Orleans to throw and try and keep up. That bodes well for Kamara's role as the pass-catcher, though Etienne was also targeted enough. If Estimé takes more of a back seat next week, that would help Etienne's prospects as a fantasy RB2/3. But until we see it, it's tough to trust anyone here.

Estimé can likely be dropped if he's on your roster. Kamara should continue to have a role on third downs and the red zone, but isn't anything more than a flex in PPR. Etienne is also in that territory, a risky RB3/flex in PPR who is becoming one of the bigger busts for fantasy managers this season.

The Jets didn't put up much of a fight against the Bills at home in a 31-12 loss. New York failed to find the end zone and barely flirted with the red zone. So when you consider those factors and look at how the RB room shook out, it's not all that bad for Hall, who went for over 100 yards. Most of that damage was in the passing game, which is encouraging. Hall had a similar showing in his return from injury in Week 9.

But the issue is how this offense is trending, which is in the wrong direction. QB Geno Smith left in the second half and was replaced by rookie Cade Klubnik. He wasn't terrible for being thrown into the fire against a superior opponent, but if Smith misses time, this offense could struggle to score. What it would mean, however, is that the Jets would need to lean on Hall and Allen more.

Even if that's the case, and Allen continues to get around 5-10 touches per game, it won't be enough unless he finds the end zone (which may be tough). Hall now has 18 and 15 touches in the past two games, both lopsided losses. Allen has seen his passing role evaporate with the return of Hall, which was to be expected.

The Jets face the Chargers in Week 11, a team winless going into MNF in Week 10. New York also has gettable matchups against the Dolphins, Broncos and Cardinals after that. That lines up well for Hall's fantasy managers, returning to reliable RB2 status. The situation isn't great for Allen, but he could bring home some flex value in those softer matchups. Not to say the Jets will blow out or even win any of those games, but they should be competitive depending on the QB situation. Allen is still worth rostering as insurance for Hall and someone who may have some spike weeks if he finds the end zone.

For whatever reason, the Colts decided to hold onto Taylor for the rest of the season, placing him in a timeshare with the rookie McGowan. Yep, your guess is as good as mine. We won't get into the lack of a trade, but focus more on the split, which we had been seeing prior to the deadline.

It was the fourth straight game Taylor failed to reach 20+ fantasy points, which is the barometer we'll set for him given his history. He did make it to double-digit figures, which is fine, but not if you invested such a high pick in the back. Instead, McGowan found the end zone and leeched plenty of carries, though JT still nearly got to 20 touches. That's most likely a product of the matchup and Indy's passing game (or lack thereof).

Daniel Jones and the passing game continue to struggle. Go figure, a passing game got worse after dealing its top-two targets at the deadline (Keenan Allen, Josh Downs). What makes it even better is the Colts won! They're clearly trying to rebuild and improve their draft stock but failed to do so after the deadline.

Anyway, getting back on track here, it's frustrating that Taylor will have to likely continue being in a split with McGowan. But Indy also has no choice but to run the ball a ton. JT is still getting paid a ton, so he should still maintain around 10-20 touches per game. That gives him a floor, but is there a ceiling anymore? It's definitely going to be tougher to come by in this offense, but Taylor can still rip off explosives.

Taylor is no longer a certified RB1 for fantasy. But he's still startable as an RB2/3, and maybe we even see some spike weeks if he can find the end zone or rip off a long run. McGowan has now found the end zone in back-to-back games to reach double-digit fantasy points. He should be added off the waiver wire if he's still available. The Colts could rest Taylor later in the season once they're eliminated from playoff contention. When that happens, it could be McGowan's backfield, a potential league-winner.

articles.title: Social media golf star Salim Sirur apologizes after 'drunken' Internet Invitational meltdown as Dave Portnoy delivers brutal verdict on 2027 return
articles.summary: Social media golf star Salim Sirur, also known as Salim The Dream, has apologised after his drunken behaviour during Dave Portnoy’s Internet Invitational
articles.body: Social media golf star Salim Sirur, also known as Salim The Dream, has apologised after his drunken behaviour during Dave Portnoy’s Internet Invitational golf tournament drew criticism. Sirur admitted that he put drinking ahead of his teammates and the match, saying he had let down Big John and Ryan Whitney. The influencer also shared an update on his recovery, revealing that he has not consumed alcohol since the tournament was filmed and is now 90 days sober. He accepted responsibility for his actions and said he regretted how he appeared in the episodes.Salim Sirur takes responsibility for drinking during Internet InvitationalSirur represented Team Red alongside Big John and Ryan Whitney at Big Cedar Lodge in Missouri. During the fifth episode of Barstool Sports’ golf series, he was seen taking several shots of tequila. His drinking continued during the competition, and his behaviour became difficult for his teammates to handle.Following the backlash, Sirur addressed what happened in an apology video. He made it clear that he had failed to give his team the attention it deserved.‘I’m just going to get straight into it. I fed up,’ Sirur said. ’I fed up big time. I prioritized drinking over focusing on the match and focusing with my teammates.‘I really want to apologize to Big John and Whitney, for me to just only think about drinking in that situation and not focus.’He also apologised to viewers who wanted to see a competitive finish.‘Also, I want to apologize to the fans. I know you guys expected a very competitive match in episode 6. And, like I said, I prioritized drinking over that.’The influencer then shared an important update about his decision to stop drinking. He explained that the tournament had been filmed months earlier and that August 13, 2026, was the last time he consumed alcohol.‘I had a huge problem back in the day. This was filmed three months ago, and I’m 90 days sober today. I haven’t drank since that last EP, which was August 13th, 2026.’Sirur also spoke about watching his own behaviour on screen. Although he initially found parts of Episodes 4 and 5 funny, he was unhappy with what he saw when he looked at the footage again.‘Taking a look back at it and really seeing how I was, I don’t like seeing myself that way. That wasn’t a good representation of myself.’He further said:‘I want to let everybody know too that I am doing really well,’ Sirur continued. ‘Obviously right now I have to relive this situation, and, you know, I deserve all of it. I deserve everything that’s coming to me. I deserve all the hate. I deserve all the comments.‘I deserve know, all- everything. I deserve everything. So if you guys want to give it to me, give it to me. I put myself in this position. I did it to myself, and, you know, I got to take accountability for it.’He thanked Barstool Sports for including him in the tournament and expressed hope that he would get another opportunity.‘I hope to get invited next year… something like this will never happen again.’Dave Portnoy rules out Salim Sirur’s return for 2027However, Sirur’s hopes of returning may face a major obstacle. Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy has already made his position clear about the influencer’s participation in the 2027 competition.‘Salim’s a nice kid and I hope he gets the help he needs,’ Portnoy said in a video. ‘But my god he fing ruined it the final match … It’s selfish to every motherfer there to do what he did. He will NOT be back next year. If he is, I’m OUT.’Portnoy’s comments make it clear that Sirur’s apology has not changed his decision. articles.title: Grand Slam of Darts: Beau Greaves and Jonny Clayton knocked out at the group stage
articles.summary: Beau Greaves' win over Niels Zonneveld is in vain as she is knocked out of the Grand Slam of Darts because of Saturday's heavy defeat by Luke Littler.
articles.body:
Beau Greaves was eliminated from the Grand Slam of Darts at the group stage despite ending her campaign with a win over Niels Zonneveld in Wolverhampton.

Greaves, 22, beat Dutchman Zonneveld 5-3 but it was not enough to keep her in the competition after Saturday's heavy defeat by Luke Littler .

The three-time women's world champion fought back impressively from 3-1 down, winning three consecutive legs to take the lead in the best-of-five match.

She missed two match darts in a tense final leg but 28-year-old Zonneveld could not capitalise, failing to take out 154 before Greaves finished with double eight to seal the victory.

Zonneveld will face defending champion Littler next and will need to beat him 5-2 or better in order to progress instead of the world number one.

Earlier in the day, Rob Cross started his campaign with a crushing 5-1 win to eliminate fifth seed Jonny Clayton, who suffered back-to-back defeats.

Clayton claimed the first leg but Cross surged back to win five in a row and finished with an average of 114.32, including three 180s.

Sixth seed Ross Smith was also knocked out despite edging a 5-4 thriller against German Gabriel Clemens.

The pair were neck and neck at 4-4 before Smith won the deciding leg, but his defeat by Rusty-Jake Rodriguez on Saturday meant that he could not qualify.

Northern Ireland's Josh Rock, who was eighth seed, is also out after defeat by Kevin Doets, while 15th seed Luke Woodhouse has been also eliminated.

articles.title: Week 10 Booms and Busts: Patrick Mahomes, Chiefs showcase best fantasy football outing — without Kenneth Walker III
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Scott Pianowski examines the winners and losers of Week 10's Sunday action.
articles.body:
Although the Chiefs have been contenders all year, the shape of this offense has always felt different. New running back Kenneth Walker III has been the star. Signature QB Patrick Mahomes has played well, but in a secondary role. The offense has been missing splash plays downfield. More often than not, this KC team wore you down and beat you up, but other than the Walker highlights, it hasn't been especially pretty.

And then came Week 10. With Walker unavailable, the Chiefs ironically showed their best offensive form in two months.

Mahomes was just about perfect in a 35-13 romp at Atlanta, completing 22-of-35 passes for 348 yards and five touchdowns. He was only sacked once — on several plays he had ridiculous time to throw — and didn't turn the ball over.

The Chiefs kept hitting haymakers downfield. Seven different players had a catch of 20 yards or more, and Mahomes spread his touchdowns around to four teammates. Josh Downs (4-53-1) produced in his first KC start. Cyrus Allen (2-44-1) got behind the Atlanta defense for a 39-yard score. Andrew Armstrong made the most of a late target, turning it into a circus catch for a 43-yard touchdown. Rashee Rice (5-82-0) didn't score, but he had a rare downfield chunk play, a nifty 50-yard grab on a contested route. Some days, it feels like everything works.

And then there's rookie Emmett Johnson, the replacement for Walker (groin). Johnson is obviously one of the biggest Week 10 winners. The rookie racked up 171 total yards (101 yards rushing, 70 receiving) and caught a couple of touchdown passes. The first was a win for play design, the second a classic case of Mahomes making something when the original options aren't there. Everyone knows how special Walker has been this year, but Johnson's a league-tilter if Walker isn't available. Both players are fun to watch.

So now we wonder when Walker might be back, and if Johnson can maintain some kind of role when Walker plays. Johnson now has four touchdowns in three weeks, and he had six touches in both Weeks 8 and 9. Walker's job is obviously secure, but Johnson might be too good to ignore moving forward. Perhaps the rookie can hold deeper flex value in the final third of the year.

For as muted as Mahomes has looked at times this year, he hasn't been bad. He was the QB7 before this week started. He rarely turns the ball over. The Cardinals are a favorable draw next week, and the Buffalo matchup in Week 12 could turn into a pinball game.

The one big name from the Chiefs who missed this party was Travis Kelce. The Hall of Fame-bound tight end had an early 23-yard catch but dinged his ankle on the play and missed some time in the game. He eventually finished with two catches for 30 yards. He's now gone six straight weeks without a touchdown catch, though he did have a scoring run last week. He's on the starting fringe for the rest of the fantasy season.

The Dallas defense has been awful all year, but the Niners really took this unit behind the woodshed Sunday. San Francisco finished with 584 yards of offense in a glorious 46-40 win, the type of day where everything comes in for fantasy.

Start with Christian McCaffrey, who had two long touchdowns catches and another scoring run, part of a silly 223-yard day. Deebo Samuel Sr. only had six touches, but two of them went for touchdowns — one by air, one by land. Brock Purdy was harassed at times by the Dallas pass rush (five sacks) but otherwise a wizard, throwing for 389 yards and three scores (he also had a couple of nifty scrambles). And if you needed to try a Hail Mary in the backfield, Kaelon Black came through (11-53-1, plus 2-13-0 receiving).

George Kittle managers are a little bit disappointed, although 6-74-0 is never a bad tight end haul. Keenan Allen (5-61-0) was a quick study, and Jordan Watkins (2-49-0) got downfield for two splash plays. Unfortunately for the Niners, it's back to work the next two weeks: the Vikings and Seahawks come to San Francisco.

So the Dallas carnival was alive and well. Although the Cowboys never seemed to be a threat to win this game, their offense showed up, too. Dak Prescott threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns, and George Pickens (11-145-3) rewarded everyone with a short memory. CeeDee Lamb needed that late touchdown, but a 7-71-1 line is just fine. Ryan Flournoy (5-59-1) remains one of the best third receivers in the league. Note that 24 of Prescott's 30 completions went to his three-top wideouts — that's the type of narrow concentration we live for.

Maybe the Cowboys won't get a pinball game from the Titans and Eagles the next two weeks (although Tennessee had the quarters ready against Jacksonville on Sunday). But there are some fun matchups tied to Dallas the rest of the way. Note their schedule from Week 13 onward: at Seahawks, bye, at Rams, Jaguars, Giants. Let's keep attacking this defense as often as we can.

The Rams were another offense that had everything working in Week 10, despite Puka Nacua and Davante Adams not being available. Matthew Stafford threw for three touchdowns and the offense racked up 202 rushing yards. The 34-6 win over the Cardinals was never competitive.

Okay, maybe everything wasn't working. While Blake Corum (17-100-1) was excellent throughout and Ronnie Rivers (15-81-0) cleaned up in garbage time, Kyren Williams (12-23-0 rushing, 2-9-0 receiving) could never get started. Williams is still a good player, of course, but it's possible Corum is taking over this backfield. The Rams will have a lot of other things to think about as they enter their Week 11 bye.

There are no adequate descriptors to fairly praise Jahmyr Gibbs. He's just unfair. The NFL's best back had a 252-yard party against the Patriots in Germany, scoring twice and scoring over 40 points in some fantasy formats. It was his second-best rushing output of the year and his best receiving work (7-99-0). The rest of the Detroit schedule isn't 100% sunshine and lollipops — the Buccaneers come calling next week, and the Vikings host them in Week 15, two nasty draws. But just about everyone else on this schedule — depending on what you think of the Bears — is either a gettable opponent or a defense to exploit. Praise the fantasy gods who gave you the No. 1 slot three months ago.

Chuba Hubbard continues to smash as one of the best middle-round picks of the year. He turned 32 touches at New Orleans into 172 total yards and two scores, helping the Panthers escape with a key NFC South win. Hubbard even excelled on plays that were washed out — he lost one touchdown and some second-level runs because of penalty. The Carolina offensive line has been hurt at times this year, but nothing has stopped Hubbard. He'll do his thing at home against Baltimore next week.

The only defense that's been stopping Trevor Lawrence this year has been his own — the Jaguars have several blowout wins this year and often Lawrence has been pulled early for practical reasons. So fantasy managers appreciated the Titans fighting back Sunday; the Jags took the 40-23 win, and Lawrence was able to enjoy a full afternoon (three touchdowns, 352 passing yards, and a season-best 27 rushing yards). It was also fun to see top WR Parker Washington get the type of workload he deserves (7-152-1, nine targets).

Lawrence is working his way into the MVP chat, and should do well against the Giants and Titans (again) the next two weeks. Are the Jaguars the AFC favorites right now?

Man, do the Patriots need next week's bye. They were not competitive in Sunday morning's 35-10 thumping by the Lions, in part because Drake Maye (ankle) was hurt early. But it's starting to look like a lost season for A.J. Brown, who had just two catches for 27 yards and eventually left with a new hamstring injury. Corey Kiner (10-25-0) and Rhamondre Stevenson (6-4-0) went nowhere against the sturdy Detroit front.

Green Bay's offense hit the skids in a 30-10 loss to Minnesota, but this feels like a result you throw out. The Vikings are a horrible matchup for most offenses. Jordan Love (eight sacks) was under siege from the creative Brian Flores blitzes, and the Packers couldn't consistently run the ball, same as always. The Rams will be a challenge for Green Bay next week, and Love and friends should certainly do well against the Saints and Bills after that. No major rank changes needed.

The Saints hate the first period more than Jeff Spicoli. New Orleans has a piddly nine first-quarter points this year, and zero touchdowns. The Sunday loss to Carolina fit the script — New Orleans was scoreless at halftime before cramming 17 points into the second half. The backfield was a three-headed mess with Travis Etienne Jr. returning — Etienne had a mediocre 34 total yards on 11 touches, and Audric Estimé (7-6-0) was bottled up. Sure, Alvin Kamara somehow turned five touches into two short touchdowns, but good luck getting that story to continue.

At least rookie Jordyn Tyson (11-80-0) looked excellent on 13 routes, showing he's finally ready to be trusted as a heavy-rotation player. Just stay healthy, kid.

articles.title: Cam Ward posts another encouraging outing in Week 10 vs. Jacksonville
articles.summary: Cam Ward continued to show signs of improvement in Week 10, passing for 231 yards and running for 39 more against Jacksonville.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans QB Cam Ward completed 28 of 39 passes for 231 yards with two touchdowns and one interception in Week 10 against the Jacksonville Jaguars . He ran three times for 39 yards.

Why It Matters: Fantasy managers are trying to determine if Ward can be a viable asset, although he is starting to redeem himself after a rough start to the season. Ward threw for two touchdowns for the second consecutive game - accounting for as many passing scores as he had over the team's first seven contests combined. Ward, who threw for a career-high 304 yards in Week 8 against Cincinnati, is a low-end QB2 option at best most of the time, but he has a favorable matchup in Week 11 against a porous Dallas Cowboys pass defense.

articles.title: Chargers vs. Ravens: 4 bold predictions for Week 10 matchup
articles.summary: Here are four bold predictions for the Chargers’ Week 10 contest against the Ravens.
articles.body:
The Chargers weren't so quiet this past week during the trade deadline.

After reports surfaced that they would stand pat, the Bolts made one trade. However, it was rescinded.

Daiyan Henley is back with the Chargers after the trade with the Broncos fell through. After all that, the Bolts have the same team heading into Week 10 when they face the Ravens .

Los Angeles is the league's only winless team. They are 0-8, but they have a great opportunity to get their first win over the hobbled Ravens.

If these four things happen, the Chargers could possibly get a win.

Daiyan Henley records a season-high in tackles

It was a whirlwind of a week for the Chargers linebacker. First, Henley finds out he was traded from the team that drafted him four seasons ago to their division rival, the Broncos. And a little over 24 hours later, the trade fell through after a failed physical. Henley is back with the team now, and I think he will be out for blood. Last week, Henley recorded a season-high 10 tackles against the Texans . I think he set another season-high in primetime against the Ravens.

Chargers keep Derrick Henry under 100 rushing yards

The Chargers' run defense ranks in the bottom half in that category, allowing an average of 122 rushing yards per game. Through eight games, the Chargers have allowed 11 rushing touchdowns. Los Angeles will face their toughest test yet with running back Derrick Henry. It's been tough sledding for Henry over the past few weeks, and I think that trend continues. Henry has rushed for under 60 yards in four consecutive games.

The Ravens will have yet another quarterback under center: veteran Jacoby Brissett. The Chargers' defense has been the team's only bright spot. Their offense and defense haven't provided enough complementary football this season, but forcing turnovers could help change that. Brissett has had a mixed -to-rough time taking care of the football this season. Los Angeles will take care of that.

Justin Herbert has his best game of the season on primetime

Justin Herbert is playing the worst football of his NFL career. He's coming off another disappointing performance against Houston, throwing for 193 yards and one touchdown in a 44-22 loss. However, Herbert has a chance to play his best game yet against an inconsistent Ravens defense. Baltimore is allowing 329.7 passing yards per game, and while Herbert has yet to reach 300+ passing yards, that will happen in front of a national audience.

articles.title: Tony Pollard amasses 99 total yards, TD in Week 10 against Jaguars
articles.summary: Tony Pollard was stymied by Jacksonville's elite run defense in Week 10, but he still managed 99 total yards and a touchdown in Week 10.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans RB Tony Pollard carried nine times for a season-low 33 yards but added eight catches for 66 yards and a touchdown in Week 10 against the Jacksonville Jaguars .

Why It Matters: Pollard ran for 246 yards and five TDs the previous two weeks after scoring one TD in the first seven games. He was held in check on the ground against Jacksonville's elite run defense but posted season highs in receptions and receiving yards to go with his first pass TD catch of the season. Pollard will have a chance for another big game in Week 11 when he plays against his former team, the Dallas Cowboys, who gave up a franchise-record 584 yards and 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers this week.

articles.title: Wan’Dale Robinson unable to get anything going in Week 10 vs. Jaguars
articles.summary: Wan’Dale Robinson turned in his third game of the season with 10 receiving or less in Week 10, finishing with exactly that many against Jacksonville.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans WR Wan'Dale Robinson caught three of four targets for just 10 yards in Week 10 against the Jacksonville Jaguars .

Why It Matters: Robinson, who injured an ankle in this game, was held to 10 yards or fewer for a third game this season. Robinson is averaging only 7.2 yards per reception and has scored three touchdowns, so he's at best WR5 option. However, going against a poor Cowboys pass defense in Week 11 might make him useful in deep leagues.

articles.title: Elic Ayomanor posts career-high 79 yards receiving vs. Jaguars in Week 10
articles.summary: Elic Ayomanor enjoyed the best game of his young career in Week 10 against Jacksonville, tallying 79 yards on five catches.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans WR Elic Ayomanor caught five of 10 targets for 79 yards in Week 10 against the Jacksonville Jaguars .

Why It Matters: Ayomanor, who had a big play of 50 yards, set career highs in catches and yards in this one - the team's second straight game with Carnell Tate. The effort comes one game later than fantasy managers hoped, as it was hoped that Ayomanor would fill in for Tate better than he did in the team's last game (Week 8), when he could muster only three catches and 34 yards. If Tate misses another game with an injury in Week 11, Ayomanor could be worth using as a flex option against a vulnerable Dallas Cowboys defense.

articles.title: Player grades: Thunder get much-needed 125-103 win over Kings
articles.summary: Player grades for the Oklahoma City Thunder's 125-103 win over the Sacramento Kings.
articles.body:
Jamming on the brakes, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had Malik Monk flying in the opposite direction. The two-time MVP went with the killer crossover move before he drilled the outside jumper. It was all fun and games in a much-needed low-stress night.

The Oklahoma City Thunder snapped a rare three-game losing streak with a 125-103 win over the Sacramento Kings . They were in firm control throughout the night in this almost wire-to-wire victory.

Against the literal worst team in the league, the Thunder had fun in rookie mode. It didn't take long for them to get ahead. The ball movement was crisp. Isaiah Hartenstein found Kenrich Williams on a cutting layup. They had a quick 13-4 lead to get things started.

Gilgeous-Alexander went right at several Kings defenders to get the nifty up-and-under layup. Domantas Sabonis played like a guy who is trying to sabotage his way out of Sacramento. The Thunder had a 32-24 lead after the first quarter.

If you thought the Kings didn't have at least one counterpunch in them, think again. They went on an 18-7 run. The Thunder struggled to get any offense going as Gilgeous-Alexander rested. Ajay Mitchell and Nikola Topic couldn't properly run the second unit.

After Sacramento tied things up at 47 points apiece with a little under four minutes to go, Gilgeous-Alexander took over. The Thunder had a strong finish to the first half. They finally figured out the Kings' gimmicky zone defense. On their defensive end, Alex Caruso turned into a ball-hawk as he disrupted passing lanes and generated steals.

The Thunder had 30 points in the second quarter. They had a 62-50 lead over the Kings at the halftime break. To show how disoriented Sacramento is, it fouled Micah Peavy on a heave before the buzzer. Considering how this season-long road trip had played out, you'd take that score in a heartbeat. It was badly needed as the OKC fanbase's morale was at an all-time low.

The second half was much the same story. The Thunder kept their distance on the scoreboard. Gilgeous-Alexander ensured that as he almost walked his way to an efficient 40 points. He completely dissected Sacramento's defense. Darius Acuff Jr. tried his best to go band for band, but to no avail. None of its youth or offense-first guards had a shot at slowing him down. Funnily enough, maybe Nique Clifford could've been their best shot.

The Thunder had an easy 32 points in the third quarter. They had a 94-80 lead over the Kings. The final frame turned into Clifford's revenge stretch as he had nine points. As Gilgeous-Alexander sat out the final dozen minutes, OKC's B and C squad actually ballooned their advantage to a game-high 27 points. They had 31 points in garbage time.

The Thunder shot 52% from the field and went 10-of-31 (32.3%) from 3. They shot 23-of-28 on free throws. They had 21 assists on 46 baskets. Six Thunder players scored double-digit points.

Gilgeous-Alexander led the way with an efficient 37 points and two assists. Aday Mara recorded a 16-point, 13-rebound double-double. Mitchell had 14 points and five assists. Caruso finished with 11 points and four steals. Jared McCain chipped in with 12 points and Williams had 10 points.

Meanwhile, the Kings shot 45% from the field and went 14-of-43 (32.6%) from 3. They shot 15-of-20 on free throws. They had 27 assists on 37 baskets. Six Kings players scored double-digit points.

Acuff Jr. put up plenty of shot attempts with 26 points on 25 shots. Sabonis had 11 points and 11 rebounds. Monk had 14 points and 10 assists. Dylan Cardwell tallied 10 points and six rebounds. Daeqwon Plowden went off for 13 points. Leaky Black finished with 12 points and nine rebounds.

Back to business as usual for the Thunder. Now, you shouldn't throw parades because they had a stress-free win over the worst team in the league, but it shows a pulse. Something you couldn't have proclaimed after a recent bad stretch. Gilgeous-Alexander helped them gain a little confidence. Also helped that Mitchell returned. The offense was awesome — something you've seldom been able to say since the Post-D.C.C. (Dub, Chet, Caso) era started.

On an island with Alex Karaban, Gilgeous-Alexander's eyes widened like a Looney Tunes cartoon. He toyed with the fresh-faced rookie as he yo-yo'd the ball. Going with the between-the-legs move, not even Acuff Jr.'s ill-advised help made a difference. The two-time MVP stepped through to go up for the layup in a circus-style finish.

Gilgeous-Alexander finished with 37 points on 13-of-20 shooting, two assists and two rebounds. He shot 4-of-5 from 3 and went 7-of-7 on free throws.

Vintage Gilgeous-Alexander showed up once again. The Kings had absolutely no hope of slowing down the two-time MVP winner. The dysfunctional bunch was at his mercy. He completely sliced them up like a surgeon. Barely needing to break a sweat, his shot diet returned to getting to the cup or drilling pull-up jumpers. When he was on the floor, the Thunder ran the Kings out of their own quarter-filled gym.

Gilgeous-Alexander had a dozen points through the first quarter. He sat at 21 at halftime. As the Thunder ran away on the scoreboard, he flirted with another 40-burger before sitting out the final frame. Against the worst and most disorganized defense in the league, things were too easy as he went at half speed. No need to go all out against a team where half-effort was adequate.

I mean, not much to say about this one. Gilgeous-Alexander has normalized these types of super-efficient scoring outings. Especially against a basement-dwelling team. He's mastered the art of scoring in basketball. At all four levels, too — at the rim, in the mid-range, from the outside and at the free-throw line. It speaks to his NBA excellence that nobody even blinks when he has these types of video-game-esque games.

Setting a screen, Mara received the ball at the high nail. He waited for Nikola Topic to run the backdoor cut to get the easy assist. The 21-year-old continues to accelerate his player development amid the Thunder figuring out what exactly they have left with their undermanned group.

Mara finished with 16 points on 8-of-11 shooting, 13 rebounds and three assists.

Naturally, lottery-picked NBA rookies are going to have plenty of ups and downs. A rollar-coaster-esque first year is expected. And after a couple of dips that exposed how Mara just isn't ready to anchor a defense at all times, he showed why his unique 7-foot-3 frame gives him such a high floor to work out in the NBA as a rotation player at worst.

The Thunder continue to feature Mara in their halfcourt offense. About every one of their ball-handlers knows by now his galaxy-sized catch radius. Just throw it up top and odds are, he'll come down with it for an easy alley-oop connection. Not just that, but he's also a mean putback machine. The Kings didn't possess the height or muscle to slow him down on the glass.

Mara flexed his rebounding with a double-double. That included eight on the offensive boards. As the game got out of hand, he experimented with his playmaking. That has been an underutilized aspect of his game. Even if he's been extremely green at times, he's been a blessing to OKC's current injury-depleted situation. Who knows where this team would be without his frontcourt depth? Probably at a much more dire spot.

Swiping at an unproven ball-handler, Caruso punked the ball out of Plowden's possession. He single-handedly created another steal and a fastbreak bucket as the Kings failed a simple inbounds play. The 32-year-old was on another level both with his savviness and active hands.

Caruso finished with 11 points on 3-of-6 shooting, three assists and two rebounds. He shot 1-of-3 from 3 and went 4-of-4 on free throws. He also had four steals and one block.

The activity from Caruso was off the charts. Even more so than usual. Could you tell the Thunder treated this as kinda a must-win situation? As they navigate their new grim NBA reality, he's been a bright spot. Anytime he's been on the floor, it's given OKC a glimpse into the past with an all-time defensive rampage. He bullied the poor Kings' ball-handlers all night.

This will get lost in his NBA career arc, but Caruso was at the peak of his defensive powers in this one. He helped the Thunder pile up on the scoreboard. They were a plus-21 in his 18 minutes off the bench. Nice to see him get to double-digit points, but any offense is just found money. His value is at the defensive end. And that has been more important than usual right now with all their absences.

Receiving Williams' pass, Mitchell had things going with a catch-and-shoot outside jumper. The Thunder desperately missed him during his two-game absence. The 24-year-old didn't even need to have a monstrous night to get this one — just his mere presence supplied breathing room to everybody on offense.

Mitchell finished with 14 points on 6-of-14 shooting, five assists and three rebounds. He shot 1-of-4 from 3 and went 1-of-1 on free throws. He also had two steals.

Over their last two losses, the Thunder needed somebody else whom they could trust with the ball. Jared McCain was too hit-or-miss and the other candidates just weren't NBA-level scoring talent, sadly. At least not yet with guys like Bennet Stirtz. In came Mitchell. He helped OKC get ahead in the early stages of this lopsided matchup. Just the threat of another go-to scorer helps run a much smoother offense that was previously gummed up.

Back to barreling into the rim. Mitchell won't ever stray away from that blue-collar style of hoops. Even if it means missing time every now and then. He also relied on his pull-up jumper to get buckets. The Thunder need him to suit up from here on out. He's scaled up in the scoring totem pole. And has become too important at work to miss time.

Jab-stepping his way to the baseline, Clifford had Black bite on the pump-fake. The 24-year-old hopped off the floor for a one-legged mid-range jumper that swished in. Revenge bucket to start garbage time. Let's throw the new guy a shoutout as he played against his old squad for the first time since being traded.

Clifford finished with nine points on 3-of-4 shooting and three rebounds. He shot 0-of-1 from 3 and went 3-of-4 on free throws. He also had one steal.

Heading into the night, Clifford's return to the Kings was a much-discussed storyline. After all, it had only been a week since the Kings traded him for two future second-round picks. Surely, the wounds were still fresh. But as the game progressed, it felt like he was going to have a quiet night but enjoy a win. That was until he scored nine points in the final frame of inconsequential basketball.

Funny enough, Clifford had his best stretch since he joined the Thunder. The offense went from being a black hole to at least intriguing with a few layups. The defense was solid. Still early in his time in OKC, he hasn't shown a ton of promise yet. But expect him to get more opportunities as the season progresses. The Thunder need NBA talent right now.

articles.title: 5 Chargers players to watch in Week 10 vs. Ravens
articles.summary: Here are five Chargers players to watch for in their primetime matchup against the Ravens.
articles.body:
The Chargers are set to play in their first primetime game of the 2026 season.

It's finally arrived, but the Chargers are far from the team many predicted they'd be this season. Los Angeles is the only winless team in the NFL and ranks among the bottom in many major offensive categories.

Although the Chargers sit at 0-8, Monday offers a chance to get their first win of the season. If the Chargers want any chance at a win, these five players may need to have one heck of a game.

Here are the five players to watch for in Monday night's contest.

All eyes will be on Henley, the only player who was traded prior to the deadline, before the deal fell through. After a whirlwind week for the linebacker, we'll watch how he responds.

Herbert has been abysmal thus far through the first eight games of the season. Frankly, the whole offense has been atrocious. However, Herbert and that side of the ball have a chance to turn things around against his former defensive coordinator, Jesse Minter. Their familiarity is no small thing. It'll be interesting to see if Herbert can play well and finally put together a complete offensive performance.

Mack didn't play his final game as a Charger last Sunday. This season could be Mack's last, and it will likely come without a playoff win. With Lamar Jackson out and Jacoby Brissett in, the Chargers have a chance to make life difficult for the Ravens ' offense. Mack needs to generate pressure without allowing the Ravens to exploit LA's defense on the ground.

With Ladd McConkey out, the Chargers' young wide receiver could become Herbert's go-to target. Harris ranks second in receiving yards (262) and first in receptions (21). If McConkey is unavailable or limited, Harris could get more targets and a chance to establish himself as one of Herbert's most dependable receivers.

Tart has been one of the Chargers' better run-stopping defensive linemen, recording 12 run stops and 17 total tackles through eight games. He and the defensive line will have their hands full with Derrick Henry in the Ravens' backfield. If Tart continues his stellar play and keeps the Ravens' offense in check, stopping Henry must be a top priority.

articles.title: Hamilton won't accept what Leclerc 'normalised' at Ferrari says ex-F1 team boss
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton refuses to accept the strategic mistakes that Charles Leclerc has 'normalised' at Ferrari, according to ex-Formula 1 team principal Otmar Szaf...
articles.body:
Lewis Hamilton refuses to accept the strategic mistakes that Charles Leclerc has 'normalised' at Ferrari , according to ex-Formula 1 team principal Otmar Szafnauer.

Ferrari's hierarchy this season has faced much criticism for its handling of their two drivers who have had a number of on-track clashes, most notably on the opening lap at both the Italian and Mexico City Grands Prix. The drivers resolved tensions during a chat before the Brazilian Grand Prix weekend, although team principal Fred Vasseur insists that the guidelines between the two drivers at Ferrari remain the same.

However, former Alpine and Aston Martin team principal Szafnauer, and former Ferrari race engineer Rob Smedley, have addressed the team's strategic mistakes while speaking on the High Performance Racing podcast. In Singapore, Hamilton refused to pit when Ferrari called him in, suggesting a lack of faith in the decisions made by the team, even though he ultimately dropped from P2 to P6 as a result.

Former Ferrari race engineer Smedley said: "If you look at, say Mercedes and Red Bull's race management against Ferrari's over the last four years, it will have been better."

In response, Szafnauer said: "It could very well be that Lewis came from an environment where they got it right most of the time. Leclerc only knows Ferrari. So, Lewis is not venting his frustration but saying, 'Hey, I know it can be done better', whereas Charles is used to it, normalised [it]."

Leclerc is in his eighth season with Ferrari, with the team's strategic calls consistently coming under question during his time with the team. Hamilton meanwhile joined Ferrari in 2025, after 12 years with Mercedes in which he won six of his seven drivers' titles, and the team claiming eight consecutive constructors' titles.

Smedley points to two years of frustration for Hamilton

Smedley believes that Hamilton's recent grievances towards his team come off the back of 'two years of frustration'.

He said: "If you've got a team which is really working well together, you know, brilliant people, brilliant technology, brilliant tools, you've got to be getting it right eight out of 10 times. And I think he's come from an environment [at Mercedes] where they've got it right eight out of 10 times. So, this is now his frustration that he's wearing on his sleeve."

Meanwhile, Smedley has also dismissed claims that Hamilton has received preferential treatment at Ferrari from chairman John Elkann.

Speaking on the High Performance podcast, the Brit said: "There aren't factions inside Ferrari. I can tell you that. I know them. John Elkann is not favouring Lewis."

Smedley explained that Ferrari's internal structure places Elkann at the top, followed by team principal Fred Vasseur and Lorenzo Giorgetti, who oversees the commercial side of the organisation. He emphasised that the drivers are part of the same system rather than operating within competing groups, with everyone ultimately expected to contribute to Ferrari's overall objectives.

"There is a hierarchy, which is John Elkann, Fred, and then the two drivers, and everybody just works for the team, including John. So, there are no factions there. Let's not make stuff up."

When the final bell rang at The Inner Circle 38 , former ONE Bantamweight Muay Thai king Nong-O Hama had etched his name even deeper into its hallowed history.

The 40-year-old maestro conquered former ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Champion Rodtang "The Iron Man" Jitmuangnon by unanimous decision to firmly punch his ticket to the semifinals of the 2026-2027 ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Grand Prix. The marquee quarterfinal streamed live in Asia primetime for members on live.onefc.com from the fabled Lumpinee Stadium on Friday, November 13.

It was undeniably one of the most anticipated matchups in modern Muay Thai history. Two of Thailand's most beloved superstars stood face to face in the ring, each serving as the very embodiment of what the sport stands for.

Grueling wars built both legends, and time, triumph, and hard-earned lessons eventually turned those relentless brawlers into complete craftsmen. Their deep mutual respect was evident the moment the opening bell rang. Rodtang hunted the body while Nong-O fired probing kicks from the outside in a tense opening round that a casual observer might have mistaken for hesitation.

The #3-ranked flyweight Muay Thai contender told onefc.com:

Nong-O met that fire with patient, counter-oriented craft, catching his aggressive foe with a beautifully timed elbow.

Moments later, a pitch-perfect high left kick sent shockwaves through the combat sports world. It landed cleanly, and a man globally famed for his god-like durability went sprawling to the canvas. Pandemonium swallowed the stadium as Rodtang miraculously rose before the referee's count ran out.

The Evolve MMA and Superbon Training Camp athlete recalled:

articles.summary: Germie Bernard did not catch any of his three targets during the team's Week 10 blowout loss to the Cincinnati Bengals.

Pittsburgh Steelers WR Germie Bernard was targeted three times but did not have a reception in a Week 10 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals . Bernard did carry the ball once for 10 yards.

Why It Matters: It feels like bloom is off the rose with Bernard, who garnered fantasy attention by posting back-to-back games of 80 yards or more. Since then, the rookie has 57 yards on eight receptions over three games combined. While you can't blame it all on Bernard, the reality is that with Pittsburgh's passing attack floundering the only receiver worth rolling the dice on right now is DK Metcalf. Those in deeper leagues might want to continue holding onto Bernard, though do keep in mind that Roman Wilson (finger) and Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) could both return from IR shortly.

articles.title: ‘One-horse race’ – Bengals QB Joe Burrow’s historic performance against Steelers leads to MVP calls
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow made history in their 38-18 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers in an MVP-worthy performance. Burrow matched Peyton Manning’s l...
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow made history in their 38-18 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers in an MVP-worthy performance.

Burrow matched Peyton Manning's long-standing record for most consecutive games (five) with four or more touchdowns with his four-TD performance against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

The 29-year-old QB is emerging as the frontrunner for the MVP award this season, and this performance against the Steelers seems to have convinced everyone it's finally Burrow's year.

Joe Burrow hailed as MVP after incredible win over Steelers

Burrow ended the game going 35/44 on pass attempts for 409 yards, four touchdowns, zero interceptions and a 135.7 passer rating.

Fans think the MVP race has already been shut by Burrow amid his incredible season.

"Joe Burrow has full game stats at halftime. Yeah, this is a one-horse race for the MVP," were the thoughts of one fan .

"Hard to argue against Joe Burrow being the MVP favourite right now. Now it's time for him to actually live up to his clutch reputation in the playoffs. No excuses. 2 elite WR's, great offensive line. Get it done," said a fan .

"Again, Joe Burrow is the MVP rn. Idga- who my team is; that's just an objective football fact at this point," said another fan deeming Burrow as the MVP .

"Yeah man, give Burrow the MVP," said another fan .

"Joe Burrow has 302 yards and 3 touchdowns… In the FIRST HALF. Just give him the MVP," said one more fan vouching for Burrow's MVP case .

Burrow has a 74.7 completion percentage (254/340) this season for 2,795 yards, 27 touchdowns, and six interceptions with a 117.7 passer rating.

He leads the NFL in passing touchdowns and is among the leaders in completion percentage, passer rating, EPA, and other metrics, also ranking No. 1 on PFF for QBs this season.

Burrow is currently considered the favourite for the MVP award ahead of other QBs such as Josh Allen and Brock Purdy. If Burrow can continue this winning pace and production, it's hard to see anyone beating him out for the award this season.

articles.title: Thunder center Aday Mara’s double-double night draws Mark Daigneault eye-opening take
articles.summary: The Oklahoma City Thunder got back in the win column against the Sacramento Kings on Sunday, and rookie Aday Mara earned some high praise from head coach Mar...
articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder got back in the win column against the Sacramento Kings on Sunday, and rookie Aday Mara earned some high praise from head coach Mark Daigneault for his role in it.

Mara posted a double-double with 16 points and 13 rebounds in 25 minutes off the bench as the Thunder cruised to a 125-103 win at Golden 1 Center. The 7-foot-3 big man shot an efficient 8-of-11 from the field and added three assists.

After the game, Daigneault liked what he saw from the youngster , but he also made it clear that Mara cannot rest on one good night.

"He got into the game and played better as he went. It's a good experience for him, understanding you've got to get yourself back to the bottom of the mountain every night, and you've got to start climbing," Daigneault said after the game, via Nick Gallo of the Thunder.

Mara did much of his damage on the offensive glass, hauling in eight offensive rebounds that led to 12 second-chance points.

The rookie has been getting more opportunities lately with Chet Holmgren sidelined by a knee injury. Mara has been splitting time with Isaiah Hartenstein in the frontcourt and also posted a 10-point, 10-rebound double-double against the Portland Trail Blazers last week.

Of course, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander was the star of the show for Oklahoma City . The superstar guard poured in 37 points on 13-of-20 shooting, including 4-of-5 from deep, in just 29 minutes.

Ajay Mitchell, who returned from a two-game absence due to an ankle sprain , chipped in 14 points and five assists. Alex Caruso added 11 points and four steals, while Hartenstein grabbed 11 rebounds.

The victory snapped a three-game losing streak for the Thunder, who improved to 9-5 and wrapped up a four-game road trip, their longest of the season. Sacramento, meanwhile, dropped to 1-12 and has now lost six straight games.

Oklahoma City will return home to host the Atlanta Hawks on Wednesday.

articles.title: Rams may need to sign a center: These 4 options are available
articles.summary: The Rams lost 2 centers on Sunday, these 4 players could fill in
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams suffered a pair of injuries at the same position during Week 10's win over the Arizona Cardinals, as both starting center Coleman Shelton and backup Dylan McMahon had to leave the game and couldn't return. Sean McVay ended up moving Beaux Limmer to center and had to put backup guard Bill Murray into the game in his first appearance with the Rams.

L.A. is grateful for their bye this week, as they will have a chance for several players to heal and be ready for Week 12, including Shelton and McMahon. However, if the Rams won't get back Shelton or McMahon that soon, then McVay will need to sign a center.

Former second-round pick James Daniels is a free agent and hasn't signed with any team since the Dolphins released him in February. Despite signing a three-year, $24 million contract in 2025, it seems that Daniels is considered un-signable because … nobody has signed him. He hasn't even had a reported workout since Miami released him.

Daniels started 48 games for the Bears, then 36 games for the Steelers prior to becoming a free agent and signing with the Dolphins. Daniels tore his Achiles in 2024 and then suffered a pec injury in 2025, so he has only played in five games over the past two seasons. His injury history may have ended his career and that's why teams haven't worked him out, but could Daniels be ready for a call now?

Although he is older than Daniels, Glasgow has had more interest in him recently, working out for the Ravens on September 29. Glasgow signed a three-year, $20 million extension in 2024, so it wasn't long ago that the Lions saw him as a staple of the offensive line.

Glasgow has 103 career starts, mostly at guard but has experience at center.

Bates has been a lot more "promise" than production, starting only 21 career games despite signing a four-year, $17 million contract with the Bills in 2022. He's mostly a guard and a backup — and he hasn't signed with any team since the Bears released him in March — but if L.A. is just looking for depth he may be an option.

Brunskill is on the Chargers practice squad right now and he could be picked up by the Rams without even having to move. The veteran plays all over the offensive line, including center. He started 10 games at center with the Titans in 2024.

Picking up Brunskill may make the most sense for a cheap move that would involve a player who has already appeared in games this season. He's not going to be a star, but if the Rams need depth at center after the bye week, he could certainly do that.

articles.title: Wales must look to back up All Blacks win - Tandy
articles.summary: Wales head coach Steve Tandy challenges his side to build on their historic win against New Zealand when they host Australia next Saturday.
articles.body:
Wales head coach Steve Tandy has challenged his side to back up their wonderful win against New Zealand when they host Australia next weekend.

After beating the All Blacks for the first time in 73 years with the 35-28 win at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales will play the final game of the Nations Championship - before the play-offs - against the Wallabies on Saturday evening (20:10 BST).

Tandy says Wales will attempt to not dwell on what they achieved on Saturday against New Zealand as they aim for a third successive home win.

"We have to keep going and we've got a massive game against Australia next weekend," said Tandy.

"It's going to be a different kind of test for us after we have had back-to-back home wins.

"We've gone up another notch or another couple of levels, so it's important we back that up. It's about making sure when we come in that we're ready to work."

After defeat by England, Australia lost 15-12 against Scotland on Sunday, a result which leaves Wales fifth in the northern hemisphere table.

Wales are behind Gregor Townsend's side on points difference, with Scotland finishing their campaign against Japan.

Tandy's side have won three out of five games in the Nations Championship against Fiji, Japan and New Zealand with defeats in the summer against Argentina and South Africa.

Captain Dewi Lake has highlighted what has changed for this campaign to enable Wales to defeat New Zealand and rise one place in the world rankings to ninth.

"Our skills are better and I think we're a better team, which is credit to Steve and his coaches," said Lake.

"I think the belief is also different and the mindset has shifted.

"We've spoken about it a lot and it's probably easy sometimes to say we've changed our mindset and believe in ourselves.

"It feels different. Everybody has come in with a voice and a belief and [we] are challenging each other to get better. Ultimately that's what grows a group quickly."

Young players need space to grow - Tandy

Tandy believes Wales' young players need to be given the environment to express themselves.

"There's a young group that needed care," Tandy said.

"Those connection pieces we speak about a lot and it's something we pride ourselves on."

He highlighted players like Eddie James, Dan Edwards and, among those gaining caps and growing in confidence.

"It's trying to give them the freedom to play, because it's a tough place to play in Wales when things are not going right," the Wales head coach added.

"They're young men and we want these players to go out there and play with freedom.

"They need to have that and we believe in that support for them, because sometimes it may be a little bit of a burden.

"We've got to make sure these boys have a safe space."
